title: Mobile Engineer
description:
About Fin 

Fin is a next-generation payments platform built for high-value, global, and instant transactions. We are a Series A-stage company backed by Sequoia, Circle, and other notable investors. Powered by stablecoins, Fin enables users and businesses to move millions of dollars in seconds - whether to other Fin users, directly into bank accounts, or across crypto rails. By combining the speed of crypto with the reliability and trust of traditional finance, Fin reimagines how money moves worldwide. If banks and payment products were reinvented today, they would look like Fin.

About the Role 

We are looking for a Mobile Engineer to own our mobile experience across iOS and Android using React Native. This will be the first time many users interact with Fin, so your work will define how our product feels in the real world. You will turn messy real world payment flows into simple, intuitive interfaces, and help hide the complexity of crypto, wallets, and cross border settlement behind a smooth mobile experience.

You will work closely with the founders and the rest of the engineering team, make foundational decisions about architecture and design, and ship features from idea to production. If you care about building delightful consumer products on top of serious infrastructure, this is for you.

We value your time: our process focuses on practical system design and architectural discussions, not LeetCode grinding or unpaid take-home assignments.

Responsibilities 

- 
Own the Fin mobile app across iOS and Android using React Native, from architecture to implementation and polish.

- 
Design and implement flows that make sending, receiving, and managing money feel simple and trustworthy for everyday users.

- 
Help design secure account and custody patterns that can scale to handle meaningful balances and real world usage.

- 
Collaborate with design and product to prototype, refine, and ship new features quickly.

- 
Maintain a high bar for code quality through thoughtful architecture, code review, and testing.

- 
Work with backend and infra engineers to integrate APIs, payments, and identity or security features into the mobile app.

Qualifications 

- 
3+ years of experience building and shipping mobile apps in React Native . Deep familiarity with the Expo ecosystem and modern mobile build pipelines (EAS) is required.

- 
Strong product sense and attention to detail in UI and UX, especially for consumer facing apps.

- 
Solid understanding of mobile app architecture, performance, and offline or edge cases.

- 
Ability to work independently, set priorities, and drive projects from idea to shipped.

- 
Strong communication skills and comfort collaborating with design, product, and backend teams.

- 
Interest in payments, fintech, or crypto. You do not need to be a chain maximalist, but curiosity about the space helps.

Bonus Points 

- 
You have shipped an app from concept to production in a small team or as the primary developer.

- 
Experience in EITHER traditional consumer fintech apps (neobanks, peer-to-peer payments) OR mobile crypto wallets (Solana, non-custodial, etc).

- 
Experience with cloud platforms such as GCP or AWS.

- 
Experience deploying smart contracts on Solana or integrating with blockchain based systems.

- 
Background in security, threat modeling, or penetration testing, especially for consumer finance products.

title: Product Builder Intern - Growth (Jan-Mar 2027)
description:
Your Role

As a Product Builder Intern – Growth (f/m/d), you'll take growth initiatives from first idea to live feature—working at the intersection of technology, AI, and business, and making a measurable impact in a fast-growing fintech.

We have built a state-of-the-art setup between a headless CMS (Sanity) and a Next.js website that lets product and business builders ship features fast. For you, that means rapid experimentation: form a hypothesis, build it with Cursor and Claude, put it live, and measure what it moves.

The internship will be available from January 2027 for three (3) months, and will take place at our Berlin office.

- Build & Ship: Design, build, and launch AI-native features, conversion journeys, and landing pages on liqid.de —writing production code with Cursor and Claude, from concept to go-live.

- SEO & AEO: Improve how LIQID is found in search engines and cited by AI assistants—through structured data, content architecture, page performance, and our knowledge hub.

- Platform & CMS: Maintain and further develop our Sanity CMS and Next.js website—schemas, components, and templates—so that product and business teams can ship on their own.

- Collaboration: Partner with Product, Marketing, Design, and Engineering teams to drive initiatives forward, and share what you learn so the whole team gets faster.

What you bring

- Background: Currently enrolled in a bachelor's or master's program in Computer Science, Business Informatics, Engineering, Economics, or a related field, preferably with a focus on software, product, or design.

- Builder Track Record: You have built and shipped something real—a website, app, tool, or automation—and can show it. Share a link with your application.

- Technical Skills: You read, write, and review code with confidence—ideally JavaScript/TypeScript and React—work with Git, and use AI coding tools such as Cursor and Claude every day.

- Language Skills: Fluency in German and English .

title: Software Engineer (Product Backend) - London
description:
About Us

Teton is redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology and a great product experience. As populations get older and staff shortages grow, healthcare systems are under pressure. Our mission is to decrease the cost of healthcare while improving the quality of care.

Our product enables care teams to intervene, prevent and operate more efficiently. Our ambient sensors in resident rooms capture activity, sleep, respiration, gait and more. These signals are used both to react fast to risk events, like falls, and for long-term health analysis that care teams can act on.

Teton is scaling fast, operating in the Nordics, UK, DACH and US. We raised a $20M Series A. Expect travel to the US to meet users and team members.

We focus relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, deploying solutions at speed that make a tangible difference for carers. We are an aspiring meritocracy biased towards action, always striving to raise the bar. If you are driven by impact, speed and leveling up, this might be the place for you.

If you are looking for a 9-17 job, perform best with structure and struggle dealing with unknowns, this is not for you. We believe close collaboration between a hard-working, high-agency team enables the fastest and most efficient iteration cycles, helping us build an impactful product that healthcare professionals truly love to use.

The Job

We're looking for a talented and driven Product Engineer to own customer-facing features from the first conversation with a care team to the feature running in production. Care workers rely on our product during every shift and care managers use it to follow up on their residents, on mobile and on the web. This isn't a ticket-taking role. You'll talk to users, cut scope, build across the whole stack, and check afterwards whether what you shipped actually made a shift easier. Your goal is to shrink the time from a customer request to a deployed solution, without cutting corners on reliability or on the privacy of residents' health data.

In this role, you will focus on:

- Feature Development: Own features end-to-end, from design discussions through implementation to production rollout across multiple markets and languages, on the web app, the mobile app and the APIs behind them.

- Customer Insight: Talk to care staff and our customer success team every week, visit care facilities, and turn what you hear into clearly scoped product changes. Come with ideas, sketch the solution, and push it forward.

- Fast Iteration: Break large designs and features into small shippable pieces. Get MVPs in front of users quickly, measure how they're used, and iterate or kill them.

- Backend & APIs: Design and build the APIs, data models and services your features need. You will not just consume APIs, you will help shape, improve and fix the systems behind them.

- Quality, Privacy & Safety: Ship with care for health data: sensible access control, auditability and privacy by default. Build test coverage and use staged rollouts so new features never get in the way of the alerts care teams depend on.

Qualifications

- Strong TypeScript skills: this is the language for everything we build.

- Solid production experience with React on the web and/or React Native.

- Comfortable working across the stack: you've built backend APIs and worked with relational databases (e.g. Postgres), not just UI.

- Great product taste and a keen eye for UX. You work well with designers and can make sensible design decisions yourself when needed.

- Comfortable talking directly with non-technical users and turning messy feedback into concrete decisions.

- Previous startup experience and/or shipping a product where you owned the outcome, from idea to adoption.

- Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work both independently and in a team.

Nice to Have

- Experience with React Native and Expo in production.

- AWS or equivalent cloud platform experience.

- Familiarity with TanStack, real-time systems or push notifications.

- Experience with health data or other regulated, privacy-sensitive domains (e.g. GDPR).

- Experience shipping products across multiple markets and languages.

What We Offer

- Participation in our warrant program (stock options).

- A small team where your decisions directly shape the product.

- Work on software that healthcare workers depend on every day, the impact is tangible and immediate.

Join Our Team

We're looking for individuals who share our vision and value ownership and entrepreneurship over a conventional job.

At Teton, you'll have the chance to make a real impact with your work.

If you're ready for more than just a job, come aboard and be part of our mission to transform healthcare.

As a Senior Statistician , you’ll work within a cross-functional team alongside other analysts, data-scientists, engineers, and commercial stakeholders in generating actionable insights to help improve healthcare.

How you’ll make an impact: 

- Take ownership and evolve our existing program impact measurement capabilities, built in-house and in partnership with third-party experts such as IQVIA.

- Develop and maintain analytically rigorous program performance benchmarks.

- Discuss standard and bespoke measurement methodologies with clients during pre-sale and present analysis results to brand marketing team as well as client analytics team

- Mentor and help Business Analytics Managers with interpreting measurement results, identifying actionable insights and preparing for client discussions leading to increased sale and renewals

- Serve as statistical consultant and provide guidance to Data-Science team for advanced modeling

- Help implement and scale survey / market research based measurement capabilities 

- Manage vendor relationships for third party data procurement.

The Core Values of the Client Intelligence team 

As an organization we value diversity - in backgrounds and in experiences. Healthcare is a universal concern, and we need people from all backgrounds to help build a better future for all. Below are additional core values specific to the Insights Team.

- Collaboration —The best candidates and teammates are not only strong in their own aptitudes but care deeply about supporting each other's growth.

- Passion for Data —You’re going to help our clients and team members with data-driven decision making. We need someone that can manipulate millions of rows of data and also ask the right questions to find the important insights.

- Reliability – Our team is efficient, flexible, and agile only because we trust the reliability of each member. We need self-starters and goal-oriented individuals for our continued success.

- Curiosity – Continuous learning is a cornerstone at Doximity, and curious individuals thrive in our environment. We’re looking for someone who is curious enough about data to go above-and-beyond the task for the true insight.

- Respect – A key dynamic that allows our team to flourish is respect: for ourselves and our quality of work, for our teammates, and for our internal clients who are under the pressure of deadlines and finance goals.

About you: 

- 10+ years of professional experience in a quantitative or statistical role (e.g., statistician, biostatistician), within healthcare, pharma, or a related industry.

- Hands on experience with statistical methodologies and techniques such as test-vs-control study designs, covariate adjustment methods (e.g., ANCOVA), clustering, etc.

- Strong context into HCP prescription and claims data, including how they're recorded and tracked by data vendors, what they represent, and typical data gaps.

- Advanced SQL and python proficiency including writing complex queries across multiple tables and familiarity with data science libraries

- Experience working with third party analytics vendors such as IQVIA, including running independent studies, engaging in RFPs and contract discussions, and maintaining relationships.

- Experience applying data science techniques such as clustering and machine learning to sponsored engagement, using Rx and Dx data to measure impact.

Our engineering team is flat, with no sub-teams, so you'll work across the whole platform. We build with AI coding agents every day and expect you to do the same.

- Write evals for model-facing features and track the metrics of the workflows you ship

- Work with protected health information (PHI) safely, with least-privilege access, no PHI in logs and auditable changes

- Build and maintain the skills, plugins, MCP integrations and review bots our engineers use with Claude Code and Codex

Our stack

- Backend: Python (our primary language for new services), Kotlin with Hasura (GraphQL) on our established platform, plus TypeScript (NestJS) and some Go

- Frontend and mobile: React, Next.js, React Native

- Data: PostgreSQL (including pgvector), Snowflake

- Workflows and contracts: Temporal, gRPC/Protobuf

- Infrastructure: AWS (ECS Fargate, RDS), Terraform, GitHub Actions, Datadog, LaunchDarkly

- AI: Claude and OpenAI models, Claude Code and Codex, with our own skills, plugins, MCP integrations and an AI code-review bot

Must-haves

- 5+ years of experience building and shipping production software

- Recent, hands-on experience using or building AI harnesses: the layer around a model or coding agent (project instructions, tools and MCP servers, skills, hooks, subagents, evals), not only calls to a model API. You can show what you set up or built.

- At least one personal project you built and published on the web, live and usable by anyone, ideally a SaaS with payments working (e.g. Stripe). Share the link when you apply.

What we're looking for

- A track record of owning products or features end to end, from an unclear problem to a system people depend on

- Strong full-stack skills in Python and TypeScript, with experience across frontend, backend, databases and cloud infrastructure

- Comfort working in a large, established codebase

- Hands-on experience building with LLMs, including tool use, agent orchestration, structured outputs, retrieval and evals (LangGraph, an agents SDK or similar)

- Daily use of AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor. You know how to set them up for a codebase (project instructions, skills, MCP servers, hooks, subagents), run several tasks in parallel and review their output carefully. - High agency: you unblock yourself, look for context and ask questions when you need to

- Clear written communication. The team is distributed across time zones and most decisions happen in specs, PRs and tickets.

Nice to have

- Experience in healthcare or another regulated industry (HIPAA, payer and claims workflows, EHR integrations, HL7/FHIR)

- Temporal or another durable workflow engine

- React Native

- Running LLM evaluations or safety checks on model output in production

- Having built your own agent harness, MCP server or plugin for a coding agent

- Open-source work or internal tools that other people use

If you meet all the must-haves and most of the rest, we'd like to hear from you, even if you don't check every other box.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Tech Lead - NetBox Core
description:
NetBox Labs is seeking a Staff Software Engineer and Tech Lead for NetBox Core, a team in our Applications group.

NetBox is a product that reaches people in a few ways: our open source community runs NetBox OSS; commercial customers use NetBox Cloud (SaaS) or NetBox Enterprise (self-managed). NetBox Core builds NetBox and its core plugins, the code that runs everywhere NetBox runs. We work closely with NetBox Delivery, the team that ships NetBox and runs it on Cloud and Enterprise.

As Tech Lead, you set the technical direction for NetBox Core and stay hands-on in the code. You bring deep Django and Python skills, experience running Django in production SaaS at scale, and a good understanding of Kubernetes and SRE practices.

In this role you will: 

- 
Design and build NetBox and its core plugins, across the data model, business logic, APIs, and integrations

- 
Own the technical direction and architecture of NetBox and its core plugins, as the team's primary technical decision maker

- 
Keep NetBox fast and reliable as data and usage grow, from query performance to background jobs

- 
Drive NetBox releases, including versioning, release notes, and the release cadence

- 
Lead and mentor the team's engineers through design and code review, and set the team's standards for testing and documentation

- 
Take part in community contributions and public design discussions on GitHub

- 
Work with NetBox Delivery and the Cloud, Enterprise, and Foundations teams to build observability into NetBox, define release contracts, and drive cross-team changes through RFCs

- 
Act as a technical escalation point during incidents and make sure postmortem actions get done

Requirements: 

- 
7+ years of software development experience, including technical ownership of a production system or platform area

- 
Deep Python and Django expertise, including running a Django SaaS application in production at scale

- 
A track record of finding and fixing Django performance problems, including ORM query optimization, Postgres indexing and query plans, schema design, and migration risk on large tables

- 
Production experience with background job queues such as RQ or Celery, and message brokers such as Redis or RabbitMQ

- 
Experience building observability into applications, including error reporting, distributed tracing, metrics, and structured logging, with tools such as OpenTelemetry and Sentry

- 
A working understanding of how Python applications run on Kubernetes, and of SRE practices such as SLOs, incident response, and postmortems

- 
Experience leading engineering work without formal manager authority, including mentoring other engineers

- 
Hands-on experience building inside an AI-augmented development harness, including Claude Code and the workflows that make agentic tooling reliable

- 
A track record of making technical decisions under ambiguity and driving work across team boundaries, from writing the RFC to getting a cross-team migration done

- 
Comfort working in the open, including discussing designs in public issues, reviewing community contributions, and writing user-facing documentation

Nice to haves: 

- 
Experience building deep inside Django's internals, such as the app registry, model metadata, and the schema editor, for example to create models at runtime as our Custom Objects plugin does

- 
Experience with the parts of the Django ecosystem NetBox uses, such as Django REST Framework, GraphQL with Strawberry, django-filter, and django-mptt

- 
Experience with advanced Postgres features, such as schemas for multi-tenancy or branching, advisory locks, and connection pooling

- 
Hands-on experience with several tools in our delivery stack: AWS, Kubernetes and Helm, GitHub Actions, ArgoCD or FluxCD, Terraform, and Prometheus and Grafana

- 
Experience working in a B2B software startup or high-growth organization

- 
Familiarity with the NetBox ecosystem or network automation

- 
Contributions to or maintenance of an open source project

- 
Experience with self-managed or on-premises delivery

About NetBox Labs:

NetBox Labs helps companies build and manage complex networks. We help customers accelerate network automation by delivering open, composable products and supporting the network automation community.

NetBox Labs is the commercial steward of open source NetBox, the world’s most popular network source of truth, and Orb, the next-generation open source network observability platform. Our products include NetBox Enterprise, a fully supported self-managed NetBox with advanced features, and NetBox Cloud, a secure, scalable, and reliable SaaS edition of NetBox.

NetBox powers thousands of companies, and NetBox Labs is backed by investment from Notable Capital (formerly GGV), Grafana Labs CEO Raj Dutt, Flybridge, IBM, Salesforce Ventures, and Mango Capital.

Our culture and values: 

- 
We own and solve problems with high attention to detail.

- 
Our open source contributors, users, customers & team are all part of our community. When our community wins, we win.

- 
We prioritize simplicity and think twice before adding complexity

- 
Clear communication helps keep our team aligned and collaborating smoothly.

NetBox Labs is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe diverse teams build better software, and we welcome applicants of every race, color, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, and veteran status. If you need accommodation at any point in the process, just let us know.

title: Stage AI Developer

Technologie is bij ons geen bijzaak. We bouwen ons eigen AI-platform: On Brand. Merken leggen daarin hun huisstijl, tone of voice en richtlijnen vast. Teams maken er vervolgens sneller content mee die klopt met het merk; van banners tot complete workflows.

Als stagiair AI Development word je deel van het Creative Technology team dat On Brand bouwt. Je werkt aan echte features, niet aan een oefenproject. En je werkt zoals wij werken: met Claude Code als vaste collega. Je bent bekend met software factories, of wil hier graag over leren.

We zoeken een stagiar of werkstudent die 3 tot 5 dagen per week beschikbaar is vanaf januari of februari 2027.

Wat ga je doen? 

- Je bouwt nieuwe features voor On Brand, front-end en back-end

- Je werkt elke dag met Claude Code: je geeft heldere opdrachten, controleert wat de AI maakt en zorgt dat het werkt

- Je bouwt met Next.js en TypeScript. Github heeft geen geheimen voor jou en je bent bekend met postgreSQL, REST API's en LLM's

- Je test je werk, lost bugs op en legt vast wat je hebt gebouwd

- Je denkt mee over nieuwe AI-toepassingen voor merken en marketingteams

- Je laat het team zien wat je bouwt en leert, bijvoorbeeld in een korte demo

Wat breng je mee? 

- Je volgt een hbo- of wo-opleiding, bijvoorbeeld Software Engineering, HBO-ICT, Informatica, Creative Technology of CMD

- Je hebt een portfolio met recente webapplicaties die je zelf hebt gebouwd, met links naar een live versie of GitHub

- Je hebt kennis van en ervaring met Next.js

- Je werkt nu al dagelijks met Claude Code

- Je bent nieuwsgierig, leert snel en vindt bouwen gewoon leuk

- Je werkt zelfstandig, maar vraagt om hulp als je vastzit

- Pré: ervaring met TypeScript, Supabase of het werken met AI-modellen via een API

Wat bieden wij?

- Een vaste begeleider en regelmatig feedback op je code en je werkwijze

- Een kantoor met dakterras in de Houthavens

Solliciteren 
Herken je jezelf hierin? Stuur je cv, een korte motivatie en de link naar je portfolio of GitHub. Vertel er in een paar zinnen bij hoe jij Claude Code gebruikt en wat je er onlangs mee hebt gebouwd.

title: Founding Engineer
description:
About 3Y Health

3Y Health is building the operating system for healthcare practices, an AI-native platform that helps clinicians start, run and grow their practice. We work as a managed services organization (MSO): along with the software, our operations team runs the back office for the clinics we partner with, including billing, insurance and compliance. We currently serve applied behavior analysis (ABA) therapy practices and are expanding into speech, occupational and physical therapy, and psychiatry.

About the role

Members of Technical Staff own features end to end. You'll work with the clinicians and operators who use what we build, scope the problem, design and build the solution across the stack, deploy it and follow how it performs in production. Our engineering team is flat, with no sub-teams, so you'll work across the whole platform. We build with AI coding agents every day and expect you to do the same.

What you'll do

- Design and build AI agents and automated workflows for clinic operations, such as insurance benefits verification, prior authorizations, patient intake, claims and clinical documentation

- Build features for clinicians, patients and families, and our internal operations team, on web and mobile

- Take ambiguous problems from 0 to 1, working with operators and clinicians to define the problem, write the spec and ship a first version

- Design the services, data models and APIs behind your features and manage the infrastructure as code

- Own your services in production: deployments, monitoring and incident response

- Write evals for model-facing features and track the metrics of the workflows you ship

- Work with protected health information (PHI) safely, with least-privilege access, no PHI in logs and auditable changes

- Build and maintain the skills, plugins, MCP integrations and review bots our engineers use with Claude Code and Codex

Our stack

- Backend: Python (our primary language for new services), Kotlin with Hasura (GraphQL) on our established platform, plus TypeScript (NestJS) and some Go

- Frontend and mobile: React, Next.js, React Native

- Data: PostgreSQL (including pgvector), Snowflake

- Workflows and contracts: Temporal, gRPC/Protobuf

- Infrastructure: AWS (ECS Fargate, RDS), Terraform, GitHub Actions, Datadog, LaunchDarkly

- AI: Claude and OpenAI models, Claude Code and Codex, with our own skills, plugins, MCP integrations and an AI code-review bot

Must-haves

- 5+ years of experience building and shipping production software

- Recent, hands-on experience using or building AI harnesses: the layer around a model or coding agent (project instructions, tools and MCP servers, skills, hooks, subagents, evals), not only calls to a model API. You can show what you set up or built.

- At least one personal project you built and published on the web, live and usable by anyone, ideally a SaaS with payments working (e.g. Stripe). Share the link when you apply.

What we're looking for

- A track record of owning products or features end to end, from an unclear problem to a system people depend on

- Strong full-stack skills in Python and TypeScript, with experience across frontend, backend, databases and cloud infrastructure

- Comfort working in a large, established codebase

- Hands-on experience building with LLMs, including tool use, agent orchestration, structured outputs, retrieval and evals (LangGraph, an agents SDK or similar)

- Daily use of AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor. You know how to set them up for a codebase (project instructions, skills, MCP servers, hooks, subagents), run several tasks in parallel and review their output carefully. If you haven't heard of Claude Code, this role is likely not a fit.

- Good product sense and the ability to make solid UI decisions without a dedicated designer, using our component library

- High agency: you unblock yourself, look for context and ask questions when you need to

- Clear written communication. The team is distributed across time zones and most decisions happen in specs, PRs and tickets.

Nice to have

- Experience in healthcare or another regulated industry (HIPAA, payer and claims workflows, EHR integrations, HL7/FHIR)

- Temporal or another durable workflow engine

- React Native

- Running LLM evaluations or safety checks on model output in production

- Having built your own agent harness, MCP server or plugin for a coding agent

- Open-source work or internal tools that other people use

If you meet all the must-haves and most of the rest, we'd like to hear from you, even if you don't check every other box.

Location and employment

This is a full-time employee role, remote and based in Toronto, Ontario. This posting is for an existing vacancy.

We use AI tools to help screen and assess applications for this role.

title: Senior Software Engineer (Storage) - remote in the US
description:
Company Description

About Mirantis 

Mirantis is the Kubernetes-native AI infrastructure company, enabling organizations to build and operate scalable, secure, and sovereign infrastructure for modern AI, machine learning, and data-intensive applications. By combining open source innovation with deep expertise in Kubernetes orchestration, Mirantis empowers platform engineering teams to deliver composable, production-ready developer platforms across any environment—on-premises, in the cloud, at the edge, or in sovereign data centers. As enterprises navigate the growing complexity of AI-driven workloads, Mirantis delivers the automation, GPU orchestration, and policy-driven control needed to manage infrastructure with confidence and agility. Committed to open standards and freedom from lock-in, Mirantis ensures that customers retain full control of their infrastructure strategy.

Job Description

Overview 

Design and build the software that provisions, integrates, and operates high-performance storage for GPU-accelerated compute and AI platforms. You will develop the control-plane services, drivers, and tooling that connect enterprise and scale-out storage systems to Kubernetes-based workloads across hybrid, edge, and air-gapped deployments built on the Mirantis K0rdent stack.

About the Role 

We are looking for a software engineer who thinks in systems and data paths — someone who can reason about throughput, latency, consistency, and failure across a storage stack, then express that understanding as clean, testable Go. The right candidate has built production software against real storage systems (whether enterprise NAS, scale-out, or object), understands what makes storage fast and reliable at scale, and prefers declarative automation over manual operations. You should be self-directed, comfortable owning ambiguous problems end to end, and effective communicating technical decisions across teams.

Responsibilities 

1. Storage Software & Integration 

- Design and build control-plane services, drivers (e.g., CSI), and tooling that provision, configure, and operate storage for Kubernetes-based AI/compute workloads.

- Integrate high-performance storage platforms — Dell PowerScale, VAST, and comparable systems — into automated, declarative provisioning workflows.

- Build data-path, telemetry, and observability tooling to diagnose and resolve performance, reliability, and scaling issues.

2. Software & Automation 

- Write production-quality software — primarily in Go — with strong testing, code review, and operational rigor.

- Deliver infrastructure-as-code (Terraform/OpenTofu) and GitOps-driven pipelines (ArgoCD or Flux) for storage configuration and lifecycle.

- Support bare-metal and hybrid provisioning where storage intersects host and cluster bring-up.

3. Platform & Hybrid Delivery 

- Deliver storage integration for k0s-based Kubernetes via Cluster API (CAPI) and K0rdent management/child cluster topologies.

- Architect storage software for fully disconnected (air-gapped) environments, including local artifact/mirror connectivity (Harbor) and PKI/TLS considerations.

Qualifications

- 5+ years of software development, including production systems, with Go as a primary language.

- 5+ years building or integrating storage systems (distributed, scale-out, NAS, or object) at scale.

- Hands-on experience with high-performance storage platforms such as Dell PowerScale, VAST, or comparable technologies.

- Solid understanding of storage fundamentals: file/block/object models, throughput and latency behavior, caching, consistency, and failure modes.

- Experience with Kubernetes storage (CSI, persistent volumes, storage classes) and infrastructure-as-code.

- Strong written and verbal communication with technical audiences.

Preferred 

- Proficiency in Python and/or Rust in addition to Go.

- Experience with the Mirantis K0rdent stack (K0rdent Enterprise, K0rdent AI, k0s, MKE) and Cluster API.

- Experience developing storage for GPU/AI workloads (high-throughput data pipelines, GPUDirect Storage).

- Proven experience in sovereign or high-security air-gapped environments.

Additional Information

What does Mirantis offer you? 
- Work with an established Silicon Valley leader in the cloud infrastructure industry;

- Work with exceptionally passionate, talented and engaging colleagues, helping Fortune 500 and Global 2000 customers implement next-generation cloud technologies;

- Be a part of cutting-edge, open-source innovation;

- Thrive in the high-energy environment of a young company where openness, collaboration, risk-taking, and continuous growth are valued;

- Professional development and training;

- Attend conferences and working groups;

- Company outings, happy hours, hackathons, and tech talks;

- Receive a competitive compensation package with a strong benefits plan.

Opting out of ADMT use is requested for decisions about evaluation and review connected with the specific employment decision for the position applied for. You also have the right to appeal any decisions made by ADMT by sending your request to isamoylova@mirantis.com

title: Principal Product Security Engineer
description:
Headquarters: Remote - United States

Join the company that’s building the telemetry infrastructure for the AI era. At Cribl, we partner with IT and Security teams at many of the world’s biggest enterprises, including half of the Fortune 100, to bridge the gap between AI ambition and infrastructure reality. As the AI Platform for Telemetry, we give customers the choice, control, and flexibility to manage and analyze telemetry for both humans and agents, so they can build what’s next.

We’re one of the fastest‑growing private companies and a leading player in a massive, fast‑moving market. With a global workforce, we’re remote‑first and grounded in a simple idea: software is a people business. Cribl is the place where curious, collaborative people can do their best work, grow fast, and bring their full selves to the herd.

Why You’ll Love This Role 

Cribl is looking for a Principal Product Security Engineer to serve as a hands-on technical authority at the intersection of application, cloud, and FedRAMP environment security. You will help secure Cribl’s cloud-native, customer-managed, and hybrid products as they process high-volume data for some of the world’s largest organizations.

As a Principal engineer, impact is defined by reach. You will set long-term direction across teams, resolve critical and ambiguous security problems, advise Engineering and Product leaders, and turn security requirements into secure designs, production-ready patterns, automation, and verified outcomes. This is not a documentation-only compliance role: you will work with Engineering, SRE, Cloud Operations, Compliance, and Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) partners to make regulatory commitments real in product architecture and day-to-day operations.

This is a remote, hands-on individual-contributor role within Engineering. You will lead through expertise and influence, mentor engineers and security partners, and create durable systems that reduce risk while making the secure path easier.

As An Active Member Of Our Team, You Will… 

- Set long-term product and cloud security direction across multiple teams, shaping roadmaps, standards, secure-by-default patterns, and risk-informed design and release decisions.

- Lead Product Security Reviews for distributed, multi-tenant SaaS and customer-managed products, including architecture and design review, threat modeling, abuse-case analysis, targeted secure code review, and security test planning.

- Translate risk into concrete engineering requirements, mitigations, tests, and secure defaults; stay engaged through implementation and independently verify that the intended risk reduction was achieved.

- Serve as a principal cloud security authority across IAM and workload identity, organization and account boundaries, network exposure, KMS and encryption, secrets, logging and detection, containers and Kubernetes, serverless services, infrastructure as code, hardening, and data isolation.

- Lead the Product Security component of FedRAMP engineering. Translate FedRAMP Moderate and NIST SP 800-53 control intent into sustainable technical controls and defensible evidence, and partner on authorization-boundary and significant-change decisions, continuous monitoring, vulnerability and change management, POA&M and deviation remediation, incident response, vendor assessments, and 3PAO or assessor interactions.

- Investigate ambiguous signals and vulnerabilities from bug bounty, application and supply-chain scanners, penetration tests, cloud detections, and internal reports; determine exploitability, exposure, and impact; coordinate remediation; validate fixes and bypasses; and hunt for variants and root causes.

- Evolve scalable, risk-adaptive vulnerability management using exposure, exploitability, CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities signals, asset criticality, customer impact, and regulatory timelines,not CVSS alone.

- Build and operate durable security capabilities and developer paved roads across CI/CD, SAST, SCA, secrets, infrastructure as code, containers, cloud posture, and testing. Automate repeatable work while preserving explicit human judgment for consequential security decisions.

- Scope and oversee external penetration tests, purple-team exercises, and relevant security vendors; ensure findings become owned, verified engineering outcomes; and provide evidence-based input to build, retain, replace, or retire decisions.

- Lead multi-team work through uncertainty and high-stakes situations, making clear tradeoffs among security, reliability, delivery, customer impact, and compliance while acting with appropriate urgency.

- Communicate complex risks, options, uncertainty, and recommendations in direct, audience-appropriate terms for engineers, senior leaders, customers, assessors, and external partners; represent Cribl credibly when needed.

- Multiply the team by mentoring Product Security engineers, security champions, and engineering partners; create standards, runbooks, automation, and continuity plans that prevent critical capabilities from depending on one person.

- Evaluate and responsibly apply emerging technologies, including AI-assisted security engineering, with measurable outcomes, rigorous verification, secure operating boundaries, and clear human accountability.

- This position will require stand-by, on-call, or off-hours duties.

If You’ve Got It - We Want It 

- Typically 10+ years of relevant software security, security engineering, or software engineering experience,or equivalent demonstrated scope and impact,including substantial hands-on Application Security or Product Security and cloud security work.

- Experience securing AI or agentic systems and applying AI responsibly to security engineering workflows.

- A Principal-level track record of setting technical direction across teams, leading multi-quarter initiatives, resolving ambiguous critical problems, and influencing senior Engineering and Product leaders without direct authority.

- Deep, hands-on AWS and Azure security experience in production SaaS or cloud-native systems, including identity and authorization, network controls, encryption and key management, secrets, logging and detection, containers or Kubernetes, serverless services, infrastructure as code, and multi-tenant data isolation.

- Direct experience implementing or operating product and cloud security controls in a FedRAMP-authorized or FedRAMP-bound environment. You understand NIST SP 800-53 control intent and have supported technical control implementation and evidence, continuous monitoring, vulnerability and change management, POA&M or deviation remediation, and assessor interactions.

- Expertise leading security design reviews and threat models for complex applications, APIs, distributed systems, and cloud architectures, with the judgment to turn findings into practical countermeasures and risk-informed release recommendations.

- Strong knowledge of web and application vulnerabilities, exploit techniques, OWASP guidance, authentication and authorization protocols, cryptography, common network protocols, and secure cloud operating models.

- Ability to read production code and build maintainable automation in JavaScript or TypeScript, Python, Go, or a comparable language; willingness to work directly with Engineering to implement and verify security improvements.

- Hands-on vulnerability-response experience, including exploitability analysis, root-cause and variant analysis, remediation design, fix and bypass validation, stakeholder coordination, and incident support.

- Exceptional written and verbal communication, with the ability to make complex risk and tradeoffs clear to engineers, executives, customers, assessors, and external partners.

- A bachelor’s degree in computer science, cybersecurity, or a related field—or equivalent practical experience.

- Preferred qualifications 

- Experience securing enterprise data platforms, observability systems, high-volume data pipelines, agents, or customer-managed and hybrid software.

- Experience with AWS GovCloud, FedRAMP Moderate/High, NIST 800-53.

- Experience building developer security platforms, secure-by-default libraries, policy-as-code, or automated guardrails across SAST, SCA, DAST, software supply chain, containers, and cloud posture.

- Public security contributions such as open-source work, published research, CVE credits, standards participation, conference talks, or other demonstrated thought leadership.

- Relevant credentials such as AWS Certified Security – Specialty, CISSP, CCSP, CSSLP, GIAC, or OSCP; demonstrated practical impact matters more than certifications.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Data Platform
description:
Headquarters: San Francisco, CA or Remote (U.S.)

Location : This role is remote in the United States, Canada, or some countries in South America.

Visa sponsorship is not available for this role. 

Doximity is the leading clinical AI company with the largest network of U.S. clinicians. Doximity’s AI-powered workflow platform is trusted by over 85% of U.S. physicians and 300+ health systems. Doximity's mission is to help clinicians be more productive so they can provide better care for their patients. 

At Doximity, we value curiosity, ownership, inclusion, and a commitment to making a meaningful impact. If you're excited about solving complex problems that improve healthcare, we'd love to hear from you. 

How you’ll make an impact 

You will join the Data Services team - one of three teams in a data platform group of about ten engineers, alongside infrastructure and developer productivity.

- Work closely with data analysts, data engineers, and machine learning engineers to understand their needs - and evolve the Doximity data stack to meet them.

- Build the foundations that make client-facing data delivery safe and repeatable - per-client data isolation, access controls, and auditability.

- Build and operate the MCP-based tooling and agentic workflows through which analysts and clients interact with the data platform - and the data it manifests - by conversation rather than tickets.

- Work in a HIPAA-regulated environment where the right people and systems reach the data they need and nothing more - masking policies, scoped roles, audit trails, and approval gates that hold up to scrutiny from auditors and clients alike.

- Understand what our data product teams are trying to achieve, and design solutions that maximize the time they spend on their goals and minimize the time lost to technical hurdles.

- Help strengthen our software engineering culture within the data organization, leading by example.

- Diagnose development, performance, and stability issues in our core data pipelines and Python libraries, and help product data teams resolve problems that need platform-level expertise.

What we’re looking for 

- We’re seeking a strong Python engineer who brings deep professional experience in data engineering and internal tooling, with a track record of supporting multiple product teams simultaneously.

- Especially valuable experience:

- Snowflake beyond querying - governance features, cloning, Time Travel and Fail-safe, hybrid tables, streams, and data lifecycle capabilities, Cortex suite of AI tools, Snowpark Container Services, or data sharing.

- Kafka, change data capture (CDC) like Debezium, and database internals - a significant portion of our pipeline work lives here.

- Operating under HIPAA, SOC 2, or similar - least-privilege design, masking and de-identification, audit logging.

- Building or operating agentic and MCP-based tooling.

- Apache Airflow and AWS.

- Container-based development workflows (Kubernetes, Docker) - useful, but secondary to the above.

- We don’t expect all of these. Depth in Python, SQL, and data engineering is the requirement; the rest tells us where you’ll ramp fastest.

- The ideal candidate will demonstrate expert fluency in Python and an understanding of programming language internals.

- Advanced knowledge of software engineering practices and testing methodologies is a must; you are foremost an engineer, making you passionate about high-quality code, automated testing, and software engineering best practices. You demonstrate this both within your own team and with colleagues beyond it.

- You have deep fluency in SQL, using analytical databases, and are able to practically employ and orchestrate user defined functions, stored procedures, and other database-oriented solutions to deliver performant and cost-effective database-driven solutions.

- You have worked with data that carries real handling obligations - PHI, PII, or client-confidential data - under a framework like HIPAA, SOC 2, or GDPR. You design for least-privilege access by default, you think in terms of blast radius and auditability, and you treat these as engineering problems rather than paperwork.

- Your ability and drive to self-manage, prioritize tasks, and deliver functional solutions will be crucial to succeeding in this role.

- You treat AI-driven engineering as part of the craft, not a novelty - agentic coding tools, MCP-based tooling, and automation that removes toil - and you invest in keeping your practice current as the tools evolve. You communicate clearly in writing and in person, and you keep your work legible through practices like clear change management and well-documented code. You see your teammates as your first customer.

About Us 

- Explore our stack 

- We have over 500 private repositories in Github containing our pipelines, our own internal multi-functional tools, and open-source projects 

- We have worked as a distributed team for a long time; we're currently about 65% distributed 

- Find out more information on the Doximity engineering blog

- Our recruiting process

- 401(k) with company match

- Flexible paid time off and company holidays

- Paid parental leave

Why You'll Love Working Here 

At Doximity, you'll join a mission-driven company where your work has a meaningful impact on healthcare. We believe great ideas come from empowered teams, and we're committed to creating an environment where people can do their best work.

- Make a real impact. Help build products that support over a million healthcare professionals and ultimately improve patient care.

- Work with exceptional teammates. Collaborate with thoughtful, talented colleagues who value curiosity, humility, and continuous learning.

- Enjoy flexibility and trust. We support flexible ways of working and empower employees with the autonomy to own their work.

- Grow your career. Take on meaningful challenges, develop new skills, and shape your career through mentorship and professional development.

description:

For over 20 years, Smartsheet has empowered teams to manage work seamlessly and scale solutions smarter. Now, in our most ambitious chapter yet, we are uniting human teams with AI agents. By orchestrating the work agents do best, automating manual tasks and uncovering insights at scale, we create the space for people to focus on what truly matters: judgment, creativity, and big thinking. That is magic at work, and it’s what we show up for every day.

Smart Assist is Smartsheet's AI agent for work management, used by enterprise customers to analyze, create, and act on their work. AI Experiences builds the orchestration for Smart Assist and the user-facing implementations that expose Smartsheet's Intelligent Work capabilities to any AI surface, so users can reach the right intelligence at the right time through a coherent, reliable experience.

AI Experiences is a pillar within Applied AI, and this is a full-stack team. The work spans these areas: the Smart Assist frontend (UI components, interaction patterns, and rendering for AI experiences across Smartsheet); the Smart Assist backend and orchestrator; UX for Smart Assist tools and agents, from response formatting and onboarding to error states. On the backend, the orchestrator routes each request to the right sub-agent based on user intent, keeps conversation state across multi-turn interactions, handles fallbacks when sub-agents are unavailable, and controls feature-flagged rollout of new capabilities. We partner closely with Agent Engineering on much of this logic.

The role. You will own features and components of Smart Assist from prototype to production, across the front end, the orchestrator and back-end services. You will turn ambiguous product asks into reliable, well-measured behavior customers can trust, and work with product, design, and AI Experience to ship.

You Will: 

- Own a core piece of the Smartsheet AI experience, or a significant part of one (for example conversational analytics, chart-to-dashboard creation, or a new entry point into the assistant) from design through production.

- Build full-stack: user-facing components, the services behind them, and the contracts between the two, with typed APIs, clear error states, and tests.

- Design and ship agent tools, skills, MCP tools, and MCP Apps with contracts the model can use reliably, and decide when an action belongs in a tool, a service, or the model.

- Shape how agent output appears to users: streaming responses, loading and failure states, and handling of long or partial results, working with design and product.

- Build and evolve the Smart Assist orchestrator: intent-based routing to sub-agents, multi-turn conversation state, fallback and degradation handling, and feature-flag rollout of new capabilities, partnering closely with Agent Engineering. Populate the context the agent receives, such as user locale, timezone, and workspace state.

- Define how quality is measured for your area: build golden cases and scorers, set regression gates, and use traces and production signals to decide whether a failure needs a prompt, tool, context, or UI fix.

- Instrument features with tracing, structured logs, and latency, cost, and error dashboards, and act on what they show.

- Take part in on-call, security, and cost work for Smart Assist, shared with Agent Engineering. Reproduce production failures and review code for your team.

- Partner with PMs, designers, Agent Engineering, AI Platform, MCP, and data teams. Learn how customers use what you build and flag gaps in requirements and tests.

- Use AI coding tools to ship faster without lowering the quality bar.

What we're building next: 

Our goal for the coming year is to make Smart Assist safe to trust and hard to leave. You will help shape work across four themes:

- Be everywhere: an assistant that understands what you are looking at, such as the rows you have selected, and meets you in the flow of work, including smoother import and file upload.

- Build the habit: an assistant that remembers how you like to work, with personal, team, and organization profiles, quick commands, and a growing UI component catalog.

- Earn the trust: previews before changes apply, linked sources and explanations for results, AI edits visible in history and activity logs, and a view into the agent's reasoning.

- Work together: a directory of agents, @mentions, and the ability to save and share results as pages.

Further out, the vision is a Smart Assist that finds you before you ask: a proactive, insight-first surface that learns how your workspace works, suggests prompts personalized to you, brings in context from tools like Slack, Zoom, and documents, supports multiplayer conversations, and offers help inside the chat itself. You would help define the trust model for that experience from real customer learnings and feedback.

You Have: 

- 2–4 years of professional software engineering shipping production systems.

- Strong in Python and/or TypeScript/React, with good habits in testing, code review, and debugging.

- Experience building and shipping customer-facing features end to end, including APIs, data modeling, and user-facing behavior.

- 1+ years building LLM-powered features in production: tool or function calling, agent loops, prompt and context design, or multi-step workflows.

- Working knowledge of how agents fail (bad tool choice, context overflow, hallucinated arguments, runaway cost) and how to design around it.

- Experience designing eval scorers and golden datasets, and using results to make and defend a decision.

- Experience with MCP tools and MCP Apps, structured tool calling, or reusable agent skills.

- Comfort with production observability and with data-heavy environments (Databricks or equivalent).

- Evidence of using AI coding agents to ship faster without lowering the quality bar.

- Clear communication of quality, cost, and reliability findings to technical and non-technical audiences.

- Legally eligible to work in the U.S. on an ongoing basis.

Strong plus: 

Experience with conversational or chat UI at scale; LLM tracing tools (LangSmith, Phoenix, Braintrust or similar); prompt versioning or CI-integrated evals; dashboard, charting, or data-visualization products; enterprise SaaS permissions and entitlements; prompt-injection mitigation and output validation.

What success looks like: 

- First 90 days: ship a feature or improvement to production with eval coverage, and take your first on-call rotation.

- First 6 months: own a feature or significant part of a project with measured gains in task success, latency, or user adoption, and contribute at least one reusable component or pattern.

Why this role: 

- You build the Smart Assist experience used by enterprise customers, with real users and a measurable quality bar.

- You work across the stack, from the interface to the agent tools behind it, so you see your work reach customers end to end.

- The problems are distinctive: enterprise-grade permissions and security, and one assistant that works across a broad work-management product.

- You work on the hard parts of production agents, on a team that values engineering rigor and diverse perspectives.

At BetterHelp, you’ll carve your own path, make an immediate impact, and be challenged every day – with a supportive community behind you the whole way. 

What are we looking for? 

We're looking for a talented software engineer who enjoys solving complex problems, learning continuously, and building products that make a meaningful difference. This role is ideal for someone who has delivered multiple challenging projects, takes pride in writing thoughtful, maintainable code, and enjoys both mentoring and learning from teammates.

You'll join an engineering culture that values ownership, curiosity, collaboration, and sound technical judgment. We embrace modern engineering practices and thoughtfully adopt new technologies, including AI, to help engineers focus on solving hard problems while keeping human expertise at the center of every decision.

What will you do? 

- You will develop end to end, owning features from technical design and development through deployment, monitoring, and continued improvement.

- You will thoughtfully use approved AI-assisted development tools to reduce repetitive work, explore solutions, and improve productivity while applying your own engineering judgment to architecture, implementation, security, privacy, and code quality. Engineers remain accountable for every technical decision.

We use a mix of established and modern technologies to support a platform serving millions of users. As our products evolve, we're continually improving our architecture, modernizing portions of our codebase, and evaluating technologies that help us build secure, reliable, and scalable software.

- Backend: Linux, nginx, Laravel (PHP), MySQL, Redis

- You will NOT be limited to a narrow set of responsibilities. We encourage employees to contribute ideas, develop new skills, collaborate across teams, and explore opportunities that support both their growth and the growing needs of the business.

- You will NOT be expected to navigate a culture driven by ego or unnecessary hierarchy. We value respectful collaboration, thoughtful debate, and teammates who are committed to shared success.

- You will NOT be expected to sacrifice your well-being to make an impact. We work hard and hold ourselves to high standards, all while supporting sustainable ways of working.

- You will NOT have to wonder why your work matters. The work we do here helps to expand access to mental health care and supports people seeking help when they need it.

Can I work remotely? 

Yes. This role can be performed remotely from anywhere in the U.S. While we embrace the flexibility of remote work, we also value opportunities to bring teams together in person for collaboration and connection. BetterHelp covers approved expenses for company-requested travel, and reasonable accommodations are available for employees who are unable to travel.

Requirements

- Deep understanding of web development concepts and principles.

- Examples of full-stack projects or significant product features.

- At least one major demonstrable project that includes frontend code, backend code, and a database.

- Ability to learn quickly, navigate an established codebase, and build new skills independently.

- A strong sense of ownership and eagerness to build something meaningful.

- Three or more years of professional web development experience in any stack, solving challenging problems and implementing new features from scratch.

- Three or more years of experience with SQL, including relational schema design and complex queries.

Qualifications Expected for Position:

Bonus (Helpful, but not required)

Benefits

- Build features for clinicians, patients and families, and our internal operations team, on web and mobile

- Take ambiguous problems from 0 to 1, working with operators and clinicians to define the problem, write the spec and ship a first version

- Design the services, data models and APIs behind your features and manage the infrastructure as code

- Own your services in production: deployments, monitoring and incident response

- Write evals for model-facing features and track the metrics of the workflows you ship

- Work with protected health information (PHI) safely, with least-privilege access, no PHI in logs and auditable changes

- Build and maintain the skills, plugins, MCP integrations and review bots our engineers use with Claude Code and Codex

Our stack

- Backend: Python (our primary language for new services), Kotlin with Hasura (GraphQL) on our established platform, plus TypeScript (NestJS) and some Go

- Frontend and mobile: React, Next.js, React Native

- Data: PostgreSQL (including pgvector), Snowflake

- Workflows and contracts: Temporal, gRPC/Protobuf

- Infrastructure: AWS (ECS Fargate, RDS), Terraform, GitHub Actions, Datadog, LaunchDarkly

- AI: Claude and OpenAI models, Claude Code and Codex, with our own skills, plugins, MCP integrations and an AI code-review bot

Must-haves

- 5+ years of experience building and shipping production software

- Recent, hands-on experience using or building AI harnesses: the layer around a model or coding agent (project instructions, tools and MCP servers, skills, hooks, subagents, evals), not only calls to a model API. You can show what you set up or built.

- At least one personal project you built and published on the web, live and usable by anyone, ideally a SaaS with payments working (e.g. Stripe). Share the link when you apply.

What we're looking for

- A track record of owning products or features end to end, from an unclear problem to a system people depend on

- Strong full-stack skills in Python and TypeScript, with experience across frontend, backend, databases and cloud infrastructure

- Comfort working in a large, established codebase

- Hands-on experience building with LLMs, including tool use, agent orchestration, structured outputs, retrieval and evals (LangGraph, an agents SDK or similar)

- Daily use of AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor. You know how to set them up for a codebase (project instructions, skills, MCP servers, hooks, subagents), run several tasks in parallel and review their output carefully. If you haven't heard of Claude Code, this role is likely not a fit.

- Good product sense and the ability to make solid UI decisions without a dedicated designer, using our component library

- High agency: you unblock yourself, look for context and ask questions when you need to

- Clear written communication. The team is distributed across time zones and most decisions happen in specs, PRs and tickets.

Nice to have

- Experience in healthcare or another regulated industry (HIPAA, payer and claims workflows, EHR integrations, HL7/FHIR)

- Temporal or another durable workflow engine

- React Native

- Running LLM evaluations or safety checks on model output in production

- Having built your own agent harness, MCP server or plugin for a coding agent

- Open-source work or internal tools that other people use

If you meet all the must-haves and most of the rest, we'd like to hear from you, even if you don't check every other box.

title: Staff Backend Engineer - Search Features & APIs (SABR)
description:
About us

Launched in 2019, Constructor is an AI-first e-commerce search and discovery platform that helps shoppers find the right products at the right time and enables leading global e-commerce brands to drive meaningful revenue and conversion gains.

About the team

The SABR team owns the top layer of request processing for product discovery. We own the service that first receives product discovery requests (autocomplete, search, browse & recommendations) & executes the entire business logic that drives product discovery. That service also functions as a gateway to parse incoming user requests, orchestrate calls across the internal services that do the ranking and retrieval, interpret their responses, and assemble the final response the customer sees. We also own the public configuration APIs customers use to control how discovery behaves, and the MCP layer that exposes all of it to AI agents.

Our team owns both platform & product components: Because of the positioning of our services, we take part in every architectural decision of our core product offering. At the same time, our goals are heavily influenced by direct customer feedback, because all product discovery-related features are either implemented in or integrated with our services.

All of our services are public APIs, so interface design and backward compatibility are a constant part of the job. But most of our attention goes to keeping them fast and up: we serve up to 15k RPS, fan out to many internal services on every request, and are expected to stay available and degrade gracefully when any of them fails or slows down.

The work is distributed systems in practice rather than in theory: request orchestration, failure isolation, caching, latency budgets, capacity planning, and the observability to know what is actually happening in production. The team is small enough that engineers own problems end to end, from design through on-call.

About you

You're a staff-level engineer who wants to own systems, not tickets. You've built high-traffic, low-latency Python services and carried the pager for them. You think in trade-offs: latency versus cost, flexibility versus a public API that customers can't afford to see break, the fix that ships this week versus the architecture that has to last two years. You can lead work that spans several engineers and several quarters, you enjoy mentoring others, and you're fine when a problem shows up half-defined. You don't mind being the one who reads the spec for some unfamiliar protocol, works out how it fits, and designs an integration that holds up at scale. You change your mind when someone has a better argument, you make the people around you better, and you still care about your code long after it merges.

What you will do

- Own the technical direction of one or more of our services - architecture, performance, and reliability.

- Lead design of new systems and public APIs, and the evolution of existing ones as traffic and feature scope grow.

- Raise the engineering bar through design and code review, and mentor mid and senior engineers into owning bigger scopes.

- Partner with product, other engineering teams, and solutions/support to shape what we build and to represent search constraints and trade-offs honestly.

- Take part in on-call for the systems you own, and lead incident response and follow-through when things break.

What we are looking for

Technical

- Substantial experience building and operating high-traffic, low-latency backend services in production.

- Extensive Python knowledge (our primary language).

- Experience with observability and performance work in live systems.

- Experience designing and evolving public APIs that external customers depend on.

- Experience designing & implementing scalable service-oriented architectures.

Beyond the code

- Track record of leading projects that span multiple engineers and quarters.

- Influence without authority, and willingness to change your position when someone has a better argument.

- Clear written communication - design docs, RFCs, postmortems.

- Good judgment about trade-offs and scope.

- Comfort with ambiguity and loosely defined problems.

- Ownership that extends past merge, to how the system behaves in production.

Nice to have

- Experience with AWS

- Background in search, ranking, information retrieval, or e-commerce product discovery.

- Exposure to AI/LLM-facing infrastructure (MCP, agent tooling, or similar).

Benefits

🏝️ Unlimited vacation time - we strongly encourage all of our employees take at least 3 weeks per year

🌎 Fully remote team - choose where you live

🛋️ Work from home stipend! We want you to have the resources you need to set up your home office

💻 Apple laptops provided for new employees

🧑‍🎓 Training and development budget for every employee, refreshed each year

👪 Maternity & Paternity leave for qualified employees

🧠 Work with smart people who will help you grow and make a meaningful impact

💵 Base salary: $110k–$130k USD, depending on knowledge, skills, experience, and interview results

📈 Stock options - offered in addition to the base salary

🎉 Regular team offsites to connect and collaborate

Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion at Constructor

At Constructor.io we are committed to cultivating a work environment that is diverse, equitable, and inclusive. As an equal opportunity employer, we welcome individuals of all backgrounds and provide equal opportunities to all applicants regardless of their education, diversity of opinion, race, color, religion, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status or affiliation in any other protected group.

Studies have shown that women and people of color may be less likely to apply for jobs unless they meet every one of the qualifications listed. Our primary interest is in finding the best candidate for the job. We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet all of our listed qualifications.

How we handle your data. By submitting this application, you acknowledge that Constructor will collect and process the personal data you provide for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for this role. If you are not selected, we will retain your data for a limited period as described in our Recruitment Privacy Notice. After that period your data will be deleted or anonymized.

title: Cloud Systems Administrator
description:
Headquarters: 

URL: https://oneimaging.com 

Radiology is the second most used healthcare service, used by over 51% of the workforce annually. Despite the critical role of radiology in healthcare, the process for undergoing a medical imaging exam has remained unchanged for decades. OneImaging is solving this with a concierge approach and a premium-quality radiology network of over 5,000 vetted providers across 48 states, which also reduces imaging costs by 60-80%. Our solution helps patients and families access essential radiology services at fair prices and without surprise bills, all while delivering immediate savings and ROI for employers and payers on every exam.

The Systems Administrator owns the day-to-day administration of our SaaS and cloud vendor stack, with security and logging as the first priority. You will manage user access across every platform we use, keep audit logging and security controls configured and reviewed, write scripts to automate repetitive admin work, and act as a first responder on security incidents. You will also provide hands-on IT support to employees. This is a generalist role for someone who likes owning systems end to end: you are the person who knows how each vendor is set up, who has access to what, and where the logs live. 

What you'll do: 

Vendor and SaaS administration (security and logging first) 

- Serve as the primary administrator for our SaaS and cloud platforms: tenant settings, SSO/SAML and SCIM integration, MFA enforcement, API keys, roles and permissions.

- Configure and maintain audit logging on every platform that supports it; centralize logs where possible and make sure retention meets our compliance needs.

- Run periodic access reviews, remove stale accounts and over-privileged roles, and keep an accurate inventory of who has admin rights where.

- Own the security posture of each vendor: review security settings on new tools before rollout, track vendor security notices, and evaluate new vendor requests for risk.

User lifecycle and identity

- Onboard and offboard employees and contractors across all systems the same day, driven from Rippling and Google Workspace, our identity sources of truth.

- Manage groups, roles and licenses; keep license counts right-sized and flag waste.

- Maintain device enrollment, MDM policies and endpoint security for company laptops.

Scripting and automation

- Write and maintain scripts (Python, PowerShell, Bash) and use vendor APIs to automate provisioning, access reviews, log collection and reporting.

- Build lightweight integrations between systems (for example, HRIS to identity provider to SaaS) so manual admin work shrinks over time.

Security incident response

- Act as a first responder on security alerts: triage, contain (disable accounts, revoke tokens, isolate devices), gather evidence from logs, and escalate.

- Participate in post-incident reviews and implement the fixes that come out of them.

- Help maintain and test our incident response and business continuity runbooks.

IT support

- Provide tier 1–2 support to employees: hardware, accounts, access, video conferencing, printers and office network.

- Procure, image and manage laptops and peripherals; keep an asset inventory current.

- Write and keep up internal how-to documentation so common requests become self-service.

Platforms you will administer

These are our largest software and cloud vendors by spend over the last 12 months. Deep experience with the first group is expected; the rest you will pick up on the job.

Area

Platforms

Cloud infrastructure

Amazon Web Services (IAM, CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Security Hub)

Identity, HR and devices

Rippling (HRIS, SSO, device management) and Google Workspace, used together as our identity source of truth

Productivity and email

Google Workspace (admin console, Vault, security center)

Customer support and CRM

Zendesk, Salesforce, Intercom

Communications

Zoom, Aircall, Twilio

Data and engineering

Databricks, MongoDB Atlas, Sentry, Linear, Postman, Stytch

AI platforms

Anthropic, OpenAI (API key and usage management)

Collaboration and design

Notion, Lucid, Figma, Adobe, Scribe

Security tools

NordVPN Teams, Virtru (email encryption)

Healthcare operations

Waystar, AdvancedMD

Marketing and recruiting

Braze, ActiveCampaign, Greenhouse, LinkedIn

About you: 

- 3+ years administering SaaS and cloud platforms in a company of 50–500 people, including Google Workspace and an identity/HR platform like Rippling or Okta, and ideally AWS.

- Hands-on experience configuring SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, MFA policies and role-based access.

- Working knowledge of audit logging and log review: you know what a CloudTrail event, a Workspace audit log or a Zendesk audit entry looks like and what to do with it.

- Scripting ability in at least one of Python, PowerShell or Bash, and comfort calling REST APIs.

- Experience responding to security incidents (phishing, compromised accounts, lost devices) and documenting what happened.

- Strong IT support instincts: you communicate clearly with non-technical colleagues and close tickets fast.

- Familiarity with HIPAA or a comparable compliance framework (SOC 2, ISO 27001) and what it means for access control and logging.

Nice to have:

- AWS Certified SysOps Administrator, Security Specialty, or Google Workspace Administrator certification.

- Experience with a SIEM or log aggregation tool (Datadog, Splunk, Google SecOps, or similar) and writing detection rules.

- MDM experience (Rippling, Jamf, Kandji, Intune) and macOS/Windows endpoint hardening.

- Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code for managing AWS and SaaS configuration.

- Prior work in a healthcare or other regulated company.

- Experience administering API usage and keys for AI platforms (Anthropic, OpenAI) and setting spend and access controls.

Our business model is global, enterprise, and subscription-based. Several of our largest clients have been with us for 7+ years, and many spend $500K+/year with Testlio. 

What would your day look like? 

- Architect, develop, and deploy scalable, production-grade services directly across the core Testlio software platform.

- Author clear architectural standards and reference patterns that define domain boundaries, decoupling our current codebase into modular services.

- Partner with the Director of Engineering to execute frontend framework consolidation, improving operational performance and observability.

- Safeguard system efficiency and regulatory posture by designing with security, cost-efficiency, and ISO 27001 expectations at the center.

- Integrate secure AI/LLM patterns into customer-facing surfaces, establishing strict operational guardrails and failure modes for our Quality API.

Technical Skills 

- 15+ years of hands-on software development experience building cloud-native, business-critical platforms.

- Advanced mastery of distributed system patterns, data modeling, event-driven design, and database technologies (Relational and NoSQL).

- Proven track record designing and migrating application infrastructures, specifically moving from monolithic architectures to modular services.

- Deep experience establishing enterprise-ready patterns in AWS, emphasizing high availability, cost optimization, and secure infrastructure.

- Strong familiarity with modern full-stack code environments, including front-end web frameworks, scripting languages, and CI/CD pipelines.

- Practical, production-grade experience deploying AI/ML or LLM-based solutions with an emphasis on observable, safe automation patterns.

Human Skills 

- Fluency in English with exceptional written and verbal communication skills, especially when presenting advanced architecture concepts to business leaders.

- Ability to operate effectively as an individual contributor in fast-paced, ambiguous environments, showing proactive problem ownership.

- Strong collaboration and alignment focus, capable of guiding distributed engineering teams and technical peers without direct authority.

- Outstanding analytical thinking, balancing a broad long-term technology vision with practical, short-term implementation constraints.

- Natural inclination for remote-first work, successfully communicating and documenting technical decisions asynchronously across global time zones.

At Testlio, we aim to hire individuals who are excited about their role, thrive in a fully remote environment, and have strong long-term potential with our team. Because we are a fully distributed company, our interview process includes conversations with several team members so you can get a well-rounded understanding of the role, the people you’ll work with, and how we collaborate.
