title: Senior ML Engineer (R14284)
description:
Headquarters: Remote - India 

Who We Are 

Oportun (Nasdaq: OPRT) is a mission-driven financial services company that puts its members' financial goals within reach. With intelligent borrowing, savings, and budgeting capabilities, Oportun empowers members with the confidence to build a better financial future. Since inception, Oportun has provided more than $22.7 billion in responsible and affordable credit, saved its members more than $2.5 billion in interest and fees, and helped its members set aside an average of more than $1,800 annually. 

A Quick Note on the Role's Focus 

While the title is Senior ML Engineer , this opportunity is specifically focused on ML Platform Engineering rather than ML model development or data science.

We're looking for engineers with strong software engineering fundamentals and hands-on experience building, scaling, and operating the platforms and infrastructure that enable machine learning in production. The emphasis is on ML infrastructure, MLOps, model serving, platform reliability, and production engineering , rather than primarily developing, training, or fine-tuning ML models.

Location Note 

We’re excited to consider talent currently based in India, as well as candidates who are open to relocating to India for this opportunity. Please note that, as this is a "Remote–India" position, the role must be performed from within India. 

The Opportunity 

The Machine Learning Platform team builds the software foundations that enable data scientists and machine learning engineers to develop, validate, deploy, and operate models safely and efficiently in production. In this role, you’ll lead complex platform work from business context through production outcomes, combining hands-on engineering, architectural judgment, production ownership, and mentorship. In your first year, success means leading meaningful platform initiatives, improving reliability and developer experience, and becoming a trusted technical leader for the ML platform. 

At Oportun, we move fast and hold each other to a high bar. You’ll partner across Data Science, Product, Risk, Fraud, and Engineering to solve ambiguous problems and move the needle for members and the business.

What You'll Do 

Your day-to-day 

- You’ll lead the design, implementation, deployment, and operation of complex platform capabilities that support the machine-learning lifecycle. 

- You’ll design scalable systems for model deployment and serving, feature computation, data validation, workflow orchestration, monitoring, and production support. 

- You’ll build reusable platform components, standards, and automation while improving reliability, scalability, observability, and operational readiness across ML systems. 

- You’ll partner with Data Science, Product, Risk, Fraud, and Engineering teams to translate ambiguous business needs into practical technical solutions. 

- You’ll own significant technical initiatives end to end and lead complex production investigations—clarifying requirements, leading design, delivering safely, measuring results, and implementing durable fixes. 

- You’ll raise engineering quality through thoughtful code and design reviews, mentor engineers through pairing and technical guidance, and contribute to platform technical strategy. 

- You’ll look for ways to use AI tools thoughtfully to work smarter, reduce manual work, and make better decisions faster. 

Who You Are 

The right fit looks like this 

You do not need detailed implementation direction to be effective. Given an ambiguous problem and sufficient context, you can define the technical approach, explain trade-offs, align stakeholders, lead delivery, and own the outcome after launch. 

You’re comfortable navigating complexity and don’t wait for perfect information to move forward. You communicate clearly, give direct feedback, mentor others, and connect engineering work to member, business, and operational outcomes. 

What You Bring 

Skills & experience 

- You’ll have 5+ years of professional software-engineering experience building and operating production systems, with strong programming skills in Python and deep knowledge of API design, distributed systems, service architecture, testing, and software-design fundamentals. 

- You’ve demonstrated experience designing and operating reliable, scalable cloud-native services or data-intensive systems, with experience in ML platforms, model serving, feature engineering, data platforms, MLOps, or related systems. 

- You bring practical experience with SQL, databases, caching, and tracing data or requests across multiple systems, plus familiarity with the ML lifecycle from feature engineering and model training through evaluation, deployment, serving, monitoring, and governance. 

- You have experience with Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, Git-based workflows, and production observability, and you can evaluate technical alternatives and clearly communicate recommendations, trade-offs, risks, and dependencies. 

- You’ve demonstrated the ability to mentor engineers, improve engineering practices, lead through technical influence, and connect engineering work to member, business, product, and operational outcomes. 

Nice to Have 

- Experience with AWS, Databricks, MLflow, SageMaker, Spark/PySpark, Kafka, or streaming systems. 

- Experience building feature platforms, model-serving systems, workflow-orchestration platforms, or internal developer platforms. 

- Familiarity with monitoring model quality, data quality, feature coverage, latency, reliability, or cost efficiency, and experience working with sensitive data in a regulated or financial-services environment. 

- Experience with Java or another backend language in addition to Python, and familiarity with AI tools such as ChatGPT or Copilot to improve personal productivity. 

Our AI Mindset 

We b uild with AI. We lead with judgment. 

AI isn't a feature here. It's how we work. 

We're excited about what AI makes possible, and we're looking for people who share that curiosity. You don't need to be an expert. You need to be open to experimenting , willing to learn, and able to apply new tools in ways that actually move the needle. 

In this role, you'll be encouraged to explore AI tools, find practical use cases for your function, and bring ideas for working smarter. We believe the best outcomes come when human judgment and AI capability work together . 

Why Oportun 

What's in it for you 

Oportun offers a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to support your physical, financial, and professional well-being. Benefits vary by country of employment.

About Sezzle: 

With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We’re not just transforming payments; we’re redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we’re building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you’re excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping!

About the Role: 

We are seeking a talented and motivated, best-in-class Senior Data Engineer. This role presents an exciting opportunity to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment within a rapidly growing team, with abundant prospects for career advancement. This position will own the data pipelines, transformations, and reporting processes that support accurate, complete, and timely furnishing of customer account information to credit bureaus.

This role presents an opportunity to work in a fast-paced, high growth environment while taking hands-on ownership of a critical customer-facing data function. You will dig into account data and code, debug SQL and Python workflows, and carry issues from investigation through verified resolution. You will partner with Customer Service to resolve technical dispute escalations, with Compliance to apply approved reporting requirements, and with Engineering when a fix is needed in production services or the consumer app. We are looking for an independent problem solver who can manage recurring reporting operations while improving the systems behind them.

What You’ll Do: 

- Own recurring credit bureau furnishing operations, including data preparation, validation, submissions, bureau feedback, exception resolution, and reconciliation 

- Build, maintain, and debug SQL transformations, Python scripts, and data pipelines that produce credit reporting data

- Trace discrepancies from account activity and source records through transformation logic to furnished outputs; identify root causes and implement lasting fixes 

- Investigate escalations from Customer Service, explain what happened to account data and what should be reported under approved policies, and provide evidence to support their dispute responses 

- Identify all accounts affected by reporting defects, implement corrections and controlled reprocessing, and verify the resulting reporting outcomes 

- Develop automated tests, reconciliations, monitoring, and alerts to catch inaccurate, incomplete, duplicate, or unexpected reporting before submission 

- Partner with Engineering on defects in production services or the consumer app, providing reproducible examples, affected-account analysis, and clear requirements; validate fixes through the reporting pipeline 

- Work with Compliance to translate approved reporting requirements into technical rules and escalate ambiguous reporting scenarios 

- Document reporting logic, data lineage, procedures, and incident resolutions so the process is repeatable and can be supported by others 

What We Look For: 

- Degree in computer science, engineering, data science, or a related quantitative discipline

- 5+ years of relevant experience in data engineering or software engineering, including hands-on ownership of production data pipelines and operational workflows

- Advanced SQL skills, including complex joins, account-level reconciliation, data profiling, and troubleshooting transformation logic

- Strong Python skills, including the ability to read unfamiliar code, debug existing scripts, and implement maintainable fixes

- Demonstrated ability to independently investigate ambiguous problems, prioritize recurring operations and incidents, and carry issues through to verified resolution 

- Experience with version control, code review, automated testing, monitoring, and safe deployment and reprocessing of data workflows

- Excellent problem-solving skills, with a track record of tracing data defects across systems and preventing recurrence

- Strong business judgment and communication skills; able to explain technical findings to Customer Service and Compliance and work effectively with Engineering 

- Fluent in English

- Demonstrated experience working with Claude or equivalent large language model tools is required; candidates must be comfortable leveraging AI to enhance productivity, research, and communication.

Preferred Knowledge and Skills: 

- 
Experience with credit reporting dispute workflows, e-OSCAR, Metro 2 format, and investigating escalations from customer support teams

- 
Experience with dbt, Redshift, PostgreSQL, AWS, and workflow scheduling or orchestration tools

- 
Experience in consumer lending, servicing, payments, financial services, banking, fintech, or BNPL

The Tech You’ll Work With: 

- Python

- Redshift, PostgreSQL

- Data build tool (dbt) 

- WS, G Suite, Mac

- Coding agents Claude, ChatGPT

Interview Process: 

- Application submitted (you are here)

- Wonderlic test (30-40 min)

- Interview with recruiters (30 min)

- Verbal case study interview. Walk through a credit reporting discrepancy, trace the data and code, and explain how you would correct and prevent the issue.

About You: 

- You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed.

- You’re not bound by convention - your success—and much of the fun—lies in developing new ways to do things

- You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully.

- You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting. You have conviction and are tenacious. You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly.

- You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle.

What Makes Working at Sezzle Awesome? 

At Sezzle, we are more than just brilliant engineers, passionate data enthusiasts, out-of-the-box thinkers, and determined innovators; we are skilled musicians, yogis, cyclists, chefs, golfers, dog-lovers, and rock-climbers. title: Account Director, Public Sector (DACH)
description:
Headquarters: EMEA

Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

The Account Director will join a team driving TRM's crypto go-to-market strategy for Public Sector customers in the DACH region. Your goal will be to increase and strengthen our foothold in the space. We're looking for a customer-focused , consultative salesperson to own the entire sales process with new and existing customers. This person will be knowledgeable about the cryptocurrency ecosystem and feel comfortable navigating complex processes to close six and seven figure deals.

The impact you will have here: 

- Account Mapping — Connect with all the current key stakeholders within your territory

- Prospecting — Discover new stakeholders within your territory

- Nurturing — Own, plan, execute, and/or quarterback activities to nurture client relationships, feedback loops, referrals, renewals, upsells, cross-sells, expansions

- Account Planning — Create and execute strategic plans for your territory

- Product and Subject Matter Expertise — Hone TRM product and customer vertical subject matter expertise

- Customer Advocacy — Proactively gather and prioritize customer feedback and champion it within TRM

- Loyalty — Develop a roster of happy customers that will refer new prospects, champion TRM, and provide crucial feedback

What we're looking for: 

- At least 5+ years of experience selling SaaS products into Public Sector accounts in the DACH region

- Strong customer-facing presentation/listening skills with the ability to establish credibility with senior executives

- A knack for storytelling — ability to understand customer needs and build compelling value propositions

- Adaptable. Goals can change fast. You anticipate and react quickly.

- Autonomous, collaborative and an excellent communicator

About the Team: 

TRM's EMEA Sales Team has a fast paced, positive and open culture. Team members are given a high degree of responsibility and autonomy. The team gets together for calls regularly. Your manager tries to be available to assist you with questions, problems or at customer meetings.

Application Instructions 

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM 

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

- Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

- Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

- First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

- Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

- References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

- Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

- Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM 

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

- Accelerate repeatable workflows

- Structure and solve problems

- Improve output quality

- Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM 

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

- Priorities and targets to change quickly

- Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

- A high level of personal ownership and accountability

- Close collaboration across teams and functions

- Frequent, high-touch communication

- Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

- A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute. 

Leadership Principles 

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

- Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

- Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

- Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission 

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore. 

Privacy Policy and Additional Information 

By submitting your application, you agree to allow TRM Labs to process your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy .

We collect the information you provide (such as your resume, work history, and contact details) solely for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for current and future roles at TRM.

Because our hiring cycles for certain positions may span 24 to 36 months, we retain your personal information for up to 36 months from the date of your application. After that period, your data is deleted unless a different retention period is required or permitted by law.

If you are located in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with applicable data protection laws, you have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal data at any time before that period ends. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at privacy@trmlabs.com .

To notify TRM Labs that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form . No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

The use of AI tools of any kind (including but not limited to notetakers, interview assistants, and real-time coaching tools such as Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, Cluey, or similar) during TRM interviews is not permitted without prior approval from TRM. TRM uses its own internal tools for note-taking to ensure a consistent and confidential experience for all candidates. 

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this form .

Recruitment agencies 

TRM Labs does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to TRM employees. TRM Labs is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company without a signed agreement.

title: Architect
description:
Headquarters: Remote - US

Who we are 

At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes. We deliver innovative solutions to hundreds of thousands of businesses and empower millions of developers worldwide to craft personalized customer experiences.

Our dedication to remote-first work , and strong culture of connection and global inclusion means that no matter your location, you’re part of a vibrant team with diverse experiences making a global impact each day. As we continue to revolutionize how the world interacts, we’re acquiring new skills and experiences that make work feel truly rewarding. Your career at Twilio is in your hands.
. 

Hiring and how we work 

We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Twilions! 

Also, while we are a remote-first company, you may be asked to report in person on an ad-hoc basis for team gatherings, functional off-sites or customer meetings.
. 

See yourself at Twilio 

Join the team as Twilio’s next Architect on our Data Substrate team

About the job 

Twilio runs on data, and the platform underneath it is entering a major shift. Open table formats, the convergence of lakes and warehouses, tightening privacy regulation, and AI workloads are all changing what a data platform has to do. We’re hiring an Architect to set our direction through that shift and to make sure the systems we build over the next 3-5 years are the right ones.

You’ll own the technical strategy for our data platform, spanning storage, lake and lakehouse architecture, catalog and governance, and privacy-by-design. You’ll work across org boundaries, setting standards that dozens of teams build on and raising the technical bar for the engineers around you.

Responsibilities 

In this role, you’ll:

- Own the architecture and multi-year technical strategy for the data platform, including the lake/lakehouse, ClickHouse, Elasticsearch, and governance, and keep them coherent as one platform rather than separate systems. Define where each engine fits (for example, ClickHouse versus open table formats on object storage) and the migration path between them.

- Make and document the major design decisions (ADRs, RFCs) on storage and open table formats, catalog strategy, compute engines, tenancy, data placement, and build-versus-adopt tradeoffs, with cost and performance at petabyte scale as explicit design constraints.

- Set the reference architectures for how our core storage and query engines (ClickHouse, Elasticsearch, and lake engines) are deployed, tuned, scaled and operated as shared platforms, including capacity, cost, tenant isolation, and upgrade strategy.

- Define the reliability model for the platform: availability targets, failure domains, disaster recovery, observability, and incident response patterns that teams can adopt.

- Build privacy and compliance into the architecture, not onto it. Design deletion and right-to-erasure, retention, data residency, and PII classification so they work across the platform’s storage layers, backups, and derived datasets, including data that arrives from upstream streaming systems.

- Drive data governance: classification, catalog and metadata, lineage, access control integrated with our authentication and authorization systems, data contracts, quality and integrity standards, and a catalog teams actually use.

- Review designs and technical direction across the org, and act as the escalation point on hard distributed-systems and performance problems.

- Mentor principal and senior engineers, and grow architectural judgment across the org, not only within one squad.

Qualifications 

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

Required: 

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

- Proven track record of architecting and delivering large-scale data platforms and setting their technical strategy, on cloud infrastructure such as AWS, deployed with Kubernetes, Terraform and Helm.

- Deep expertise in storage and compute for analytical data: columnar and open table formats, lake and lakehouse architecture, partitioning, indexing, query planning, and how the choices affect cost and performance at petabyte scale.

- Proficiency in one or more of Python, Java, and Go.

- Track record of writing and driving architecture decisions across multiple teams, and of changing the direction of an organization’s technical roadmap through influence rather than authority.

- Experience elevating engineering standards and mentoring senior engineers across teams.

- Demonstrated commitment to operational excellence: architecting for high availability, observability and incident response in distributed systems, and being credible when a platform is failing in production.

- Strong written and verbal communication, including making a complex tradeoff clear to engineers and to senior leadership.

Desired:

- Experience with catalog and metadata systems (e.g., Unity Catalog, Glue, Polaris, DataHub) and open table format catalog strategy.

- Experience with a platform migration across domains or ownership models, such as moving from central to domain-owned data.

- A track record of measurable cost optimization on large data platforms.

- Networking and network security knowledge.

Location

Travel 

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, you may be required to travel occasionally to participate in project or team in-person meetings.

What We Offer

This role requires a strong combination of AI research, hands-on model training and optimization, and software engineering expertise, with the ability to translate innovative AI concepts into scalable, reliable, and practical business applications.

Working closely with software engineers, product teams, and leadership, the AI Engineer will lead the development and integration of high-performance AI solutions that solve complex business challenges, enhance operational efficiency, and deliver measurable value to our global clients.

- Train and fine-tune models using PyTorch or Keras, including data preparation and evaluation. 
- Implement and benchmark research methods before adoption.

Production & Optimization

Research & Experimentation

Working Relationships 

The AI Engineer will collaborate with:

- Global AI research and development teams. 

Success in This Role 

Success means you can build with AI and deliver reliable production solutions, not simply experiment with AI models.

- Translate research into practical engineering solutions. 
- Collaborate effectively across distributed teams. 
- Document and share technical knowledge for scalability. 
- Adapt to evolving technical and business priorities. 

Work Environment

Required Work Schedule 

This AI Engineer role requires working Monday through Friday, 7:30 PM–4:30 AM or 8:30 PM–5:30 AM IST in India, depending on U.S. daylight saving time?

The ability to consistently work the assigned schedule is a required and non-negotiable condition of this role. Candidates must be comfortable working overnight hours and maintaining reliable availability throughout the assigned shift.

Due to project deadlines, production needs, client requirements, or other business priorities, occasional weekend availability or schedule adjustments may be required. Weekend work is not intended to be the standard schedule but flexibility to support business needs when necessary is expected

Our Hiring Process

1. Initial Recruiter Screening

4. Technical / Coding Interview

- Strong engineering skills across coding, Git, testing, API/system design, and debugging.

- Production experience with LLMs, including RAG, embeddings/vector databases, and prompt/evaluation design.

Preferred Qualifications

Compensation & Benefits

title: Senior Software Engineer II, Applied AI
description:

Wrapbook is the AI platform for production finance. We’re building a system of action that puts finance teams in control of their whole production, from payroll, to spend, to accounting.

What You’ll Have:

Full-Stack Software Engineer, Internship

Open position, Berlin

Internship, 3 months

Location: Berlin (hybrid)

Start: January 2027, or as soon as you can

Format: Full-time internship, 3 months

Level: Bachelor, Master's or PhD student, or equivalent work experience

Who we are. Zeitgeist Labs is the applied research institute of the future in Berlin. Founded by scientists from Stanford, MIT, Max Planck and Charité with experience at McKinsey and in previous startups. This is a unique opportunity to join an early-stage company at its inflection point.

Problem we solve. Governments, foundations, NGOs and universities spend trillions every year on programs meant to improve people's lives. The industry that measures whether any of it works is slow and manual: months of fieldwork, hand-coded interviews, a 300 page report that lands 2 years after the program ends. The physical sciences are being accelerated by AI co-scientists. The social sciences are not, yet. In an age of ever-increasing complexity, we are building the tools that allow researchers to tackle the hardest scientific questions of our time: how societies work, and what actually changes them.

In short. You own problems end to end, working directly with the founders. Understand them, build the solution, test it, ship it. No ticket-passing.

What you'll do.

- You work directly with the founders on the system our clients use every day. You own problems end to end: understand them, build the solution, test it, ship it. No ticket-passing.

- Build and improve across the whole stack, from the research dashboard to the data layer to LLM output handling, every change shipped with a test

- Build the architecture that turns thousands of data points, interviews, surveys and papers into insights

- Extend how we collect data: interview agents, surveys, document ingestion

- Run evals when a model or prompt changes and help decide what ships

How we work.

We are a human-in-the-loop AI company. Everyone here runs a fleet of agents; the human sets the direction, makes the calls and verifies the result. Claude Code is our daily driver, specs come before code, every change ships as a pull request with tests and docs. We care about creativity, critical thinking and solution orientation, not about knowing one particular framework.

Who we're looking for.

- Self-driven: you have finished things on your own, a shipped app, a side project with users, a tool people actually use

- Critical thinker: you question what you read, including what an agent wrote for you, and can explain why a solution is right

- Wants ownership over comfort: small team, short path from your decision to the customer

Bonus points if you have.

- Built a user-facing app in some flavour of JavaScript

- Written and debugged your own SQL

- Called, orchestrated, monitored and evaluated LLMs in something you built

- A solid understanding of the German language

- An interest in philosophy, sociology, anthropology, psychology, politics or behavioural sciences in general

Why Zeitgeist Labs.

- Ownership of real problems from week one, and a piece of the architecture you can name on your CV

- Daily work with the founders, hybrid in Berlin

About the interview.

- First call with a founder

- A small technical screen: a working session in our codebase, with your tools

title: Front-End Developer
description:

Job Title: Front-End Developer
Location: Fully Remote (US)

About Edconic 

Edconic is a leading player in the alternative, experiential education space. We partner with the world's largest and most well-known brands to create and run schools that capture the legacy and value of each brand. Our students get truly unique, once-in-a-lifetime experiences that help shape their future and give them the skills they need to reach their goals.

Our Mission: 

Edconic exists to help learners stand out, move forward, and build meaningful futures in the fields that inspire them. We bring together education and industry, partnering with iconic global organizations to create transformative learning experiences. Our programs are created and delivered by educators and industry practitioners, giving learners access to professional experts, real world challenges, and practical skills. As early career opportunities shrink, we offer credibility, connections, and hands on experience that internships once provided. We prepare learners not simply for their first job but for a lifetime of growth. 

Our values 

• Transformative education: relationship-rich, experiential learning that draws out each learner’s potential.

• Belonging: a community where learners, educators, experts, and staff can bring their authentic selves and support one another.

• Stewardship: as a family-owned organization, we think in generations, developing talent, caring for our partnerships, and building an impact that lasts.

The Role 

We're looking for an experienced Front-End Developer to join our web team, which owns every Edconic digital property – from our school websites to landing pages and email templates. You'll work alongside designers, IT, and MarTech to build solutions that serve real business needs while protecting each brand's unique identity.

You'll be one of two developers on the team, working directly with our lead developer. That means real ownership of your work, a genuine voice in how we build, very little process overhead, and a codebase that is actively moving toward a modern, standardized WordPress stack. We value craft: fast pages and code that the next developer can read.

What You'll Do 

- Build and maintain public-facing websites, micro-sites, and landing pages in collaboration with our lead developer, IT, and MarTech.

- Work with UX/UI designers to confirm the technical feasibility of designs, then translate them into polished, responsive pages that stay true to each brand.

- Build and maintain custom WordPress themes across both of our stacks: modern block-based builds (ACF Blocks, core blocks, block patterns, theme.json) and established classic themes built on PHP templates, Advanced Custom Fields, and Sass.

- Collaborate with our lead developer to shape the team's coding standards, tooling, and workflow, and help migrate our existing sites toward our new modern stack.

- Stay current on emerging web standards and bring ideas to the table where they genuinely fit.

What You Bring 

- 4+ years of front-end web development experience, with strong skills in semantic HTML, CSS, JavaScript, PHP, and WordPress.

- The ability to build a custom WordPress theme from scratch using PHP templates and Advanced Custom Fields.

- Strong CSS skills across Sass and modern native CSS (custom properties, nesting), and solid vanilla JavaScript.

- Comfort working in Git/GitHub with pull requests and code reviews, and with npm-based build tools and the command line.

- A habit of writing semantic, well-structured HTML that covers accessibility basics, with an eye for reuse, cross-browser compatibility, performance, and SEO.

- Experience building and testing HTML emails.

- Strong UX/UI sensibilities and a desire to sweat the small stuff.

- A proactive, self-directed working style – you can run with a project independently and prioritize across several at once.

- Excellent written and verbal communication – you're positive, collaborative, objective, and solution-oriented.

Bonus Experience 

- Modern WordPress block development: ACF Blocks, block.json, theme.json, and block patterns.

- Composer, Bedrock or other Roots tooling (Sage/Blade, Trellis), Vite, or CI/CD with GitHub Actions.

- Deeper accessibility experience (WCAG, ARIA, assistive-technology testing).

- CRM and marketing automation integration (Salesforce, Pardot/Account Engagement).

- Multilingual WordPress sites.

- A modern JavaScript framework such as React or Vue.

- UX or UI design, and design tools such as Figma and Adobe Creative Suite.

How We Use AI 

AI-assisted development is a new and evolving part of our workflow. We use AI coding tools to speed up research, scaffolding, review, and routine work, and you're welcome to do the same.

AI is a tool here, not a substitute for expertise. You are accountable for every line of code that you ship, which means you must be able to write, review, debug, and explain production code entirely on your own. Expect to demonstrate those skills without AI assistance during the interview process.

Location, Travel & Eligibility 

- Fully remote within the United States. Occasional travel to our New York office may be required.

- Must be legally authorized to work in the US.

Our Commitment 

Edconic supports and embraces diversity and inclusiveness, and we encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply, even if you don't meet every requirement listed here. title: Growth Engineer
description:
Cresta unlocks the true potential of the customer experience, turning every conversation into a competitive advantage. Cresta’s unified AI platform combines conversational AI agents, real-time human agent augmentation, and comprehensive conversation intelligence to drive revenue and efficiency gains across every channel. The world’s leading companies, including United Airlines, Cox Communications, and Marriott, use Cresta to power world-class customer experiences every day. 

Born from the Stanford AI Lab, Cresta has raised more than $270 million from the world’s leading investors, including a16z, Greylock, and Sequoia. Cresta’s leadership includes some of the leading minds in AI today. Our CEO, Ping Wu , founded and led Google's Contact Center AI and Vertex AI platforms before joining Cresta to build the future of AI-driven customer experiences.

Over the next few years, AI is going to redefine how people all over the world interact with businesses every day. Come build that future at Cresta.

Role Overview 

As Cresta’s Growth Engineer , you'll own the systems behind how Cresta shows up on the internet. In this role, you will own the technical decisions behind cresta.com and help shape how Cresta puts its own AI agents to work for marketing use cases. You'll architect and build our web platform, create the tooling that lets marketers ship without an engineer in the loop, and develop custom AI agents on Cresta's platform. This position requires strong engineering fundamentals, high agency, and the ability to go deep in an unfamiliar domain quickly. If you are self-driven, AI-native, and eager to own something end to end, this role is for you.

Responsibilities 

The web platform

- Own how cresta.com is built end to end: how it’s structured, how content flows through it, and how it connects to everything else.

- Set the technical vision for how our website stack and CMS should evolve to meet the growing needs of our business and the rapidly changing workflows of the marketing team. Our website runs on Webflow today.

- Partner with brand and design on the interactive experiences that carry our identity. They set the creative vision; you architect and build it. Own the component system so the site stays consistent as it grows.

- Own the instrumentation where the site meets our GTM stack — forms, gated content, event tracking, and attribution — so data lands cleanly downstream, in partnership with marketing ops.

- Build the technical foundation for localization as we scale into new markets, including locale routing, URL architecture, and hreflang, partnering with our web strategy lead on CMS translation workflows and content structure

- Put in the engineering practices that let us move quickly without breaking things. Enough to ship with confidence, not so much that it slows us down.

- Ship the technical work behind our SEO and AEO programs, in partnership with the owners of those programs

AI Agent Creation

- Develop, configure, deploy, and optimize AI agents on Cresta's platform for marketing use cases, working alongside our forward deployed engineering team.

- Take agents from prototype to production, including the evaluation criteria, guardrails, and human review steps prospect-facing work requires.

- Provide a tight feedback loop to our product and engineering teams — identifying gaps, building custom tooling, and influencing the roadmap through what you learn deploying against a real audience.

What We’re Looking For 

- 7+ years working in software development, web development, AI/ML engineering, or growth engineering.

- Strong across the stack — application code, APIs, data, and infrastructure — in Python, TypeScript, Node, or similar.

- Familiarity with AI/ML concepts. Hands-on experience with large language models (LLMs), and prompt engineering techniques are strongly preferred.

- A track record of learning a domain fast and going deep. You've been dropped into something unfamiliar and become the person other people come to. 

- High agency. You define your own work, ship without being told what to build, and treat gaps as yours to close.

- Strong understanding of general AI agent frameworks, function calling, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). 

- Comfortable as the deepest technical voice on a non-engineering team, scoping ambiguous requests and explaining tradeoffs to marketers.

- Ownership. You treat the outcome as yours, including when something breaks or was built badly before you arrived.

Nice To Have 

- Experience owning a marketing website. Useful context, not a hard requirement.

- Technical SEO and AEO experience grounded in tests rather than theory.

- Marketing and GTM systems integration: HubSpot, Salesforce, Marketo, Segment, GA4, GTM.

Perks & Benefits: 

We offer a comprehensive and people-first benefits package to support you at work and in life:

- Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with plans to fit you and your family

- Flexible PTO to take the time you need, when you need it

- Paid parental leave for all new parents welcoming a new child

title: Software Engineer
description:
THE POSITION 

Our roster has an opening with your name on it

We’re looking for a Software Engineer to join our CPE Platform vertical, working within Core Products and Experiences. In this role, you’ll contribute to a multidisciplinary team building reliable, engaging products for millions of players. You’ll bring some hands-on engineering experience, a practical approach to solving problems, and a willingness to learn from and support others. You’ll help deliver well-structured software, take part in technical discussions, and contribute to documentation, collaboration, and continuous improvement across the team.

We are a growth company so there are plenty of opportunities for you to learn and grow with us, plus we have remote-first working and a generous paid leave policy to enjoy your downtime. We’re committed to making sure everyone who works here can maintain a healthy work/life balance.

THE GAME PLAN 

Everyone on our team has a part to play

- You’ll work as part of our Session Management team, helping build and improve backend services that support reliable, scalable customer sessions

- You’ll learn how our systems work and contribute to well-scoped features, fixes and improvements with support from more experienced engineers

- You’ll write clear, maintainable backend code using Java or similar languages, following team standards and best practices

- You’ll help build and improve APIs, services and database-backed functionality that can handle high volumes of traffic

- You’ll test your changes carefully and look for simple ways to make our services more reliable, observable and easier to support

- You’ll take part in code reviews, design discussions, planning sessions and team ceremonies, asking questions and sharing ideas

- You’ll investigate bugs and support issues, working with the team to understand root causes and make practical improvements

- You’ll learn about scaling systems, databases, caching and cloud infrastructure through hands-on work with the team

- You’ll keep documentation up to date so others can understand how our services work and how to support them

- You’ll collaborate closely with engineers, product partners and stakeholders to deliver changes that improve the reliability and performance of session management

- You’ll bring curiosity, humility and a willingness to learn, while growing your engineering judgement and technical confidence over time

What We’re Looking For 

THE STATS 

What we’re looking for in our next teammate

- Some experience building backend software through work, internships, placements, bootcamps, university projects or personal projects

- An understanding of Java or a similar object-oriented programming language, and an interest in developing backend services and APIs

- Familiarity with databases and SQL, with an interest in learning more about data modelling, performance and scaling

- Awareness of common data structures, algorithms and software design principles

- An interest in distributed systems, reliability, monitoring and how high-traffic backend systems operate in production

- Familiarity with cloud technologies, containers or CI/CD is helpful, but not required

- An understanding of testing basics and a willingness to write tests as part of everyday development

- Comfortable working in a team environment, asking questions, receiving feedback and learning from others

- A practical approach to problem solving and a desire to leave code and documentation clearer than you found it

- Enthusiasm for working on backend systems that support customer-facing products at scale

What You Can Expect 

- Interesting work - working in a fast-paced and ever-changing industry, new problems and exciting solutions are never too far away. There are always opportunities to learn new skills and broaden your horizons

- A sense of achievement - Our teams own their own software and when that awesome new feature ships to users and the positive feedback starts rolling in, you can feel really proud of what you and your team created

- Personal development - clear and defined career pathways for every role at every level, a supportive manager, loads of learning opportunities and even 10% of your time to dedicate to your learning.

- Belonging - everyone at FanDuel works for each other, we win together, make mistakes together and have lots of fun doing it.

- Trust - A trusting work environment where productivity is valued above all else, giving you autonomy and ownership of your time and work

- Great financial package - Including salary, bonus, pension, private healthcare, share save scheme, flexible working & holiday policy along with a number of other benefits.

ABOUT FANDUEL 

FanDuel Group is the premier mobile gaming company in the United States and Canada. FanDuel Group consists of a portfolio of leading brands across mobile wagering including: America’s #1 Sportsbook, FanDuel Sportsbook; its leading iGaming platform, FanDuel Casino; the industry’s unquestioned leader in horse racing and advance-deposit wagering, FanDuel Racing; and its daily fantasy sports product. 

In addition, FanDuel Group operates FanDuel TV, its broadly distributed linear cable television network and FanDuel TV+, its leading direct-to-consumer OTT platform. FanDuel Group has a presence across all 50 states, Canada, and Puerto Rico.

The company is based in New York with US offices in Los Angeles, Atlanta, and Jersey City, as well as global offices in Canada and Scotland. The company’s affiliates have offices worldwide, including in Ireland, Portugal, Romania, and Australia.

FanDuel Group is a subsidiary of Flutter Entertainment, the world's largest sports betting and gaming operator with a portfolio of globally recognized brands and traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: FLUT).

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion 

FanDuel is an equal opportunities employer. Diversity and inclusion in FanDuel means that we respect and value everyone as individuals. We don't tolerate bias, judgement or harassment. Our focus is on developing employees so that they reach their full potential. 

FanDuel is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please email Benefits@fanduel.com . 

The requirements listed in our job descriptions are guidelines, not hard and fast rules. You don’t have to satisfy every requirement or meet every qualification listed. If your skills are transferable and you are in the ballpark experience-wise, we'd love to speak to you!

Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

As an Intermediate Backend Engineer on the GitLab Orbit team, you'll help build and operate a graph data service that supports GitLab Duo agents, analytics, and architecture-level features across GitLab.com, Dedicated, and Self-Managed deployments. You'll join a Rust-first team that values clear ownership, thoughtful system design, and rigorous thinking about data and reliability.

The Knowledge Graph service is a Rust backend that builds a property graph from GitLab’s software development lifecycle (SDLC) and code data. It uses ClickHouse, NATS JetStream, and the Data Insights Platform. It exposes secure graph queries and MCP tools used by AI agents and product features. In your first year, you’ll take clear ownership of specific components or features (for example, parts of the SDLC indexing pipeline or query paths). You’ll help reduce single points of failure with better tests and runbooks, and you’ll help the team ship analytical services that are easier to maintain and evolve over time.

What you’ll do 

- Implement and iterate on backend features in the Rust-based Knowledge Graph service, including changes to the query engine, SDLC and code indexing flows, and API endpoints (including MCP endpoints) under guidance from senior and staff engineers.

- Maintain integrations between Knowledge Graph and the rest of the GitLab platform, working in areas that touch GitLab Rails, the Data Insights Platform (Siphon, NATS, ClickHouse), and GitLab Duo Agent Platform.

- Contribute to system design discussions by proposing options, raising questions, and documenting decisions, with a focus on reliability, scalability, and maintainability for analytical graph workloads.

- Improve the operational maturity of the service by adding or enhancing metrics, logging, runbooks, alerts, and small readiness tasks, and by participating in on-call rotation as appropriate for your level and experience.

- Collaborate asynchronously with product, data, infrastructure, security, and AI counterparts to clarify requirements, align on scope, and ship features safely for customers and sustainably for the team.

- Use AI-assisted development workflows responsibly (for example, using Knowledge Graph-backed agents and internal Duo tooling), and share what works with the team while keeping a strong focus on code quality and correctness.

- Participate in code reviews, knowledge-sharing sessions, and pairing to both learn from others and help maintain consistent standards across the codebase.

- Contribute across the stack when needed, including occasional Ruby work for Rails integration and authorization paths, or small frontend changes related to Knowledge Graph features (for example, Software Architecture Map UI plumbing).

What you’ll bring 

- Professional experience building and maintaining backend systems in production, with an understanding of reliability, maintainability, and how to support services over time (for example, incident response and follow-ups).

- Proficiency in at least one modern backend language and strong interest in Rust, with either prior Rust experience or clear evidence you can ramp quickly and deliver in a Rust-first, performance-sensitive codebase.

- Some exposure to distributed data or analytics systems (for example, OLAP databases, Kafka- or NATS-style messaging, or change data capture (CDC) pipelines), or strong motivation to develop those skills in this role.

- Interest in graph data modeling and query patterns (property graphs, multi-step (n-hop) traversals, aggregations), and willingness to learn the tools and concepts used in Knowledge Graph over time.

- Practical experience (or strong interest) using AI tools in day-to-day development, along with a thoughtful approach to validating outputs and integrating AI into your workflow.

- A language-agnostic mindset and evidence that you can pick up new languages and frameworks as needed (for example, Ruby, Go, or TypeScript/Vue where the work touches adjacent systems).

- Solid fundamentals in system design for your level, including the ability to reason about trade-offs, ask good questions, and align your implementation work with documented architectural decisions.

- Comfort working in a low-process, high-ownership environment where you take responsibility for your work, refine problem statements with teammates, and communicate progress clearly in writing across time zones in an all-remote team.

About the team 

GitLab Orbit sits within the Data Engineering organization. We work closely with partners across AI (Duo Agent Platform), analytics, infrastructure and delivery, and security because our work spans many parts of the platform.

title: Platform / DevOps Engineer
description:
Lemonway est un établissement de paiement agréé, au cœur de la nouvelle économie européenne. 

Nous sécurisons les paiements des plateformes de financement participatif, d’économie collaborative, des marketplaces et des e-commerçants, avec un fort engagement contre la fraude et pour la protection des fonds.

Réglementée par l’ACPR et bénéficiant du passeport européen dans 29 pays, Lemonway est basée à Paris et Hambourg et rassemble 150 Lemonheroes multiculturels et engagés.

Plus de 400 marketplaces nous font confiance. Nous gérons 1,4 million de portefeuilles utilisateurs et avons levé 50 M€ auprès de Breega, SpeedInvest et Toscafund.

Rentable depuis quatre ans et en croissance de +25 % en 2025, Lemonway vise à rester parmi les leaders du paiement en Europe grâce à une croissance saine et durable.

- Secteur : FinTech / Paiements en ligne

- Localisation : Paris, France (Quartier du Sentier, 2e arrondissement)

- Télétravail : Jusqu'à 2 jours par semaine (au choix)

LE POSTE 

Nous recherchons un.e ingénieur.e Platform/DevOps expérimenté.e pour nous aider à améliorer nos pipelines et nos releases afin que nous puissions fournir une plateforme fiable et évolutive à nos clients. 

En tant que membre de notre équipe Platform Engineering, tu seras amené.e à: 

- Administrer et faire évoluer les infrastructures cloud sur AWS en s’appuyant sur des services tels que ECS, EKS, S3, EC2, etc… afin de garantir la disponibilité, la scalabilité et la sécurité des environnements.

- Contribuer au maintien en condition opérationnelle (MCO) en tant que backup sur les infrastructures et services hébergés sur Azure et Google Cloud Platform (GCP)

- Maintenir et faire évoluer notre service cloud en utilisant des outils tels que Terraform et Ansible

- Concevoir, déployer et administrer des environnements conteneurisés avec Docker, tout en assurant l’orchestration et l’automatisation des déploiements applicatifs via Kubernetes et Helm.

- Assurer l’administration, le maintien en condition opérationnelle et la sécurisation des systèmes Linux et Windows Server.

- Assurer la supervision, le monitoring et l’observabilité avec Datadog, ELK et Logic Monitor

- Travailler en collaboration avec les équipes de développement pour améliorer les livraisons de code en utilisant Ansible/Gitlab CI 

- Assister en run les équipes de développement sur le projet de transition de plateforme: nous sommes actuellement sous Windows/.NET/.NETCore et nous sommes en train de passer sur Linux/NETCore/NodeJS. Nous souhaitons remplacer notre architecture monolithique par une architecture de microservices

- Garantir la sécurité, la haute disponibilité et la performance des plateformes

- Explorer de nouvelles technologies(IA, automatisation… ) tout en prenant en compte les éventuelles problématiques de sécurité

TON PROFIL 

- Tu as une expérience d'au moins 4 ans sur un poste similaire et tu maîtrises les sujets systèmes et réseaux

- Tu as une solide expérience dans la création et le développement de pipelines CI/CD et le monitoring d'environnements de production

- Tu es à l'aise avec les environnements Unix/Linux, Windows, IIS/SQLServer, et de l’expérience avec AWS (ou un autre cloud provider), Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, helm et Ansible.

- Tu es soucieux.se de la qualité, de la performance et de la sécurité du code

- Tu as idéalement travaillé sur des projets en lien avec des systèmes comme Apache Kafka, Rabbitmq...

- Tu as une appétence pour les projets open-source de grand ampleur et tu t'intéresses aux thématiques d'automatisation

- Tu parles français et anglais opérationnel 

- Tu apprécies le travail au sein d’une équipe multiculturelle et dynamique.

LE PROCESS DE RECRUTEMENT 

1) Interview RH 

Au cours du premier round, tu auras un entretien avec Sabina , Talent Acquisition Manager, afin d'explorer ton parcours et tes motivations. Ce sera également l'occasion de t'en dire plus sur Lemonway et sur l'équipe.

2) Manager Interview 

Si tu passes avec succès le premier entretien, tu auras ensuite un entretien avec Loïc , Head of Infrastructure and Security et Firas , Lead Platform Engineer. Tu auras l'occasion de discuter des missions et des attentes vis-à-vis du job. Tu seras amené.e à mettre en valeur quelques-unes de tes expériences précédentes.

3) Technical Interview 

Lors de cette étape, tu participeras à un entretien technique avec des membres de l’équipe Platform Engineering. Cet échange permettra d’évaluer tes compétences techniques, ta manière de résoudre des problématiques concrètes ainsi que ton approche des bonnes pratiques liées au poste. Tu pourras également revenir sur certains projets ou expériences techniques marquantes de ton parcours.

4) Prise de références et Offre 🍋 

NOS AVANTAGES 

- Bureaux au cœur du Sentier (Paris 2e)

- Poste hybride (2j TT / semaine)

- Carte Swile

- Mutuelle Alan

- Prise en charge à 50% du pass Navigo/Vélib

- Accès à Gymlib

title: (Senior) Web Analyst (f/m/d)
description:
Who We Are

Spread Group is a renowned global provider of customized apparel and lifestyle products, distinguished by our commitment to made-to-order technology. Our core business model revolves around producing precisely what our customers desire, precisely when they desire it. As pioneers in this space, we combine sustainability with on-demand personalization, enabling individuals and businesses to express their unique identities through bespoke creations. Join us to be part of a global leader in the exciting world of personalized apparel and lifestyle products! 

As we continue to expand our business, we are seeking a curious and passionate individual to join our team as (Senior) Web Analyst (f/m/d) and drive our business forward. 

What Will Your Role Be

We're looking for a Senior Web Analyst to own and evolve our digital measurement ecosystem. You'll help us understand how millions of users interact with our digital products and turn that understanding into better product and business decisions. You'll work at the intersection of Product, Marketing and Engineering, ensuring that our tracking is accurate, scalable and future-proof. From defining measurement strategies to implementing tracking solutions and uncovering actionable insights, you'll play a key role in improving our digital products and customer experience. 

This is not a generic Data Analytics or Data Science role. We're looking for someone with a strong background in Web Analytics, Digital Analytics, Marketing Analytics or Product Analytics who enjoys solving real business problems through reliable data. 

What You’ll Do 

- Own Digital Measurement 

- Own and continuously improve our digital measurement landscape across multiple digital products 

- Design, implement and optimise client-side and server-side tracking solutions 

- Ensure accurate, scalable and privacy-compliant data collection 

Drive Measurement Strategy 

- Translate business questions into measurement concepts and technical tracking requirements 

- Define KPIs and success metrics together with Product, Marketing and business stakeholders 

- Develop tracking specifications for new products, features and customer journeys 

Generate Insights 

- Analyse user behaviour, customer journeys and conversion funnels 

- Build dashboards and reporting solutions that enable data-informed decision making 

- Identify optimisation opportunities and provide actionable recommendations 

Experiment and Optimise 

- Design, implement and evaluate A/B tests and experimentation initiatives 

- Measure the impact of new features, campaigns and product improvements 

- Continuously improve tracking quality, measurement standards and analytics processes 

Collaborate Across Teams 

- Work closely with Product Managers, Engineers and Marketing teams 

- Present analytical findings in a clear and actionable way to both technical and non-technical stakeholders 

- Help establish analytics best practices across the organisation 

What You’ll Bring

- Several years of experience in Web Analytics, Digital Analytics, Marketing Analytics or Product Analytics 

- Hands-on experience with modern tracking implementations and digital measurement architectures 

- Practical experience with tag management systems such as Adobe Experience Platform Tags or Google Tag Manager 

- Experience with Adobe Analytics, Google Analytics 4 or comparable enterprise analytics platforms 

- Solid knowledge of JavaScript and experience with SQL and/or Python 

- Experience with client-side and server-side tracking 

- Strong analytical thinking combined with a pragmatic, solution-oriented mindset 

- A solid understanding of data quality, tracking validation and analytics governance 

- Confidence working independently while collaborating closely with cross-functional teams 

- Excellent written and spoken English 

Nice to Have 

- Experience with Product Analytics platforms 

- Experience with Looker Studio, Power BI or Tableau 

- Experience with BigQuery, Snowflake or similar cloud data environments 

- Experience with experimentation platforms 

- Knowledge of privacy regulations and consent management 

- Experience in e-commerce or digital consumer products 

Why Should You Join Us 

- Autonomy and Impact: We believe in giving people real ownership. You'll have the freedom to make decisions, take action, and see the direct impact of your work on the business. 

- Development and Growth: We believe that the greatest professional and personal growth happens when you're challenged. If you're looking to build your career, you'll find plenty of opportunities to do so. 

- We Win as a Team: Work alongside ambitious, motivated colleagues who challenge and support each other to achieve exceptional results. Through honest feedback, high standards, and shared ambition, we bring out the best in one another.

title: Software Engineer (Fleet) - London
description:
About Us

At Teton, we are redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology. Facing a global nursing shortage, our solutions offer vital support to overburdened health systems. With thousands of patient rooms across 4 countries already benefiting from our technology, we are aiming to expand to much more. We distinguish ourselves by focusing relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, rapidly deploying solutions that make a real difference.

The Job

Every patient room we deploy into puts another device on infrastructure we don't control, in a building we can't easily visit, running software that has to keep working. We're looking for an Engineer to own that problem: the systems, tooling, and infrastructure that let us ship to thousands of edge devices confidently and understand what they're doing once they're out there.

In this role, you will focus on the following areas of interest:

- Fleet Management: Build and run the systems that provision, monitor, and manage our devices in the field, from first boot in a hospital room to end of life.

- OTA & Release Engineering: Own how software gets onto devices: staged rollouts, health checks, automatic rollback, and the confidence that a bad release won't take down a ward.

- Observability: Design the telemetry, logging, and alerting that tell us a device is degrading before a nurse notices. Make remote debugging possible so we don't fly to fix things.

- Device Bring-Up & Debugging: Work with our hardware and firmware teams on new hardware revisions, reproduce field issues on the bench, and get to the bottom of problems that span kernel, driver, network, and application.

- Infrastructure & Tooling: Build the CI/CD, image builds, and internal tools that let the whole engineering team ship to hardware quickly and safely.

- Documentation: Maintain clear and detailed documentation of your work to ensure easy collaboration and knowledge sharing within the team.

Qualifications:

- Solid experience running Linux systems in production: ideally embedded or edge Linux, not just cloud VMs.

- Proficiency in Rust and/or Javascript/Typescript and/or Python

- Experience with device fleets at scale: provisioning, OTA update mechanisms (Mender, RAUC, balena, or something you built yourself), and remote access to constrained devices.

- Familiarity with Linux internals: systemd, kernel modules, device tree, networking stack, containers.

- Experience with observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or similar) and designing what to measure, not just wiring up dashboards.

- Comfortable with hardware debugging: serial consoles, working alongside hardware engineers

- Understanding of communication protocols and how devices talk to each other and to us: I2C, SPI, UART, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, MQTT.

- Pragmatism about networks you don't control: restrictive hospital IT, VLANs, proxies, flaky Wi-Fi, and long offline periods.

- Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently as well as part of a team.

- Experience with the NVIDIA Jetson platform and Linux for Tegra is a big plus.

- Experience with Yocto, Debian packaging, or custom image builds is a plus.

- Experience in the medical device or healthcare technology field is a plus.

What We Offer

- Participation in our warrant program (stock options).

- Work with state-of-the-art technology in a pioneering field.

- A vibrant, learning-focused work environment.

- A role where you can make a significant impact on healthcare delivery.

Join Our Team

We're looking for individuals who share our vision and value ownership and entrepreneurship over a conventional job. At Teton, you'll have the chance to make a real impact with your work. If you're ready for more than just a job, come aboard and be part of our mission to transform healthcare.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Performance- Weights & Biases
description:
CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com .

Weights & Biases at CoreWeave 

CoreWeave acquired Weights & Biases to create the most powerful end-to-end platform to develop, deploy, and iterate AI faster. CoreWeave operates a growing footprint of data centers covering every region of the US and across Europe, and was ranked as one of the TIME100 most influential companies of 2024. By bringing together CoreWeave’s industry-leading cloud infrastructure with the best-in-class tools AI practitioners know and love from Weights & Biases, we’re setting a new standard for how AI is built, trained, and scaled.

The integration of our teams and technologies is accelerating our shared mission: to empower developers with the tools and infrastructure they need to push the boundaries of what AI can do. From experiment tracking and model optimization to high-performance training clusters, agent building, and inference at scale, we’re combining forces to serve the full AI lifecycle — all in one seamless platform.

Weights & Biases has long been trusted by over 1,500 organizations — including AstraZeneca, Canva, Cohere, OpenAI, Meta, Snowflake, Square, Toyota, and Wayve — to build better models, AI agents and applications. Now, as part of CoreWeave, that impact is amplified across a broader ecosystem of AI innovators, researchers, and enterprises.

As we unite under one vision, we’re looking for bold thinkers and agile builders who are excited to shape the future of AI alongside us. If you’re passionate about solving complex problems at the intersection of software, hardware, and AI, there’s never been a more exciting time to join our team.

What You’ll Do: 

Performance Engineering at Weights & Biases ensures our systems and products scale seamlessly as usage grows. We embed performance thinking into every stage of development—diagnosing issues, designing scalable patterns, and building tools that empower every engineering team to deliver fast, efficient, and reliable experiences. Our mission is to make performance a shared responsibility across the company through data, automation, and collaboration.

About the role: 

As a Staff Engineer on the Performance Engineering team, you’ll take technical ownership of complex performance challenges across the W&B platform and infrastructure. You’ll design and lead experiments to improve system scalability and latency, develop standardized benchmarking and load testing frameworks, and drive initiatives to prevent regressions across product surfaces. You’ll collaborate closely with product, infrastructure, and SRE teams, combining deep technical expertise with a holistic understanding of system behavior. Day to day, you’ll blend investigation, architecture, and enablement—helping teams measure, understand, and continuously improve performance.

Who You Are: 

- 8+ years of experience as a software engineer, with at least 2 years focused on performance optimization, systems scalability, or observability.

- Proficiency in at least one of Go, Python, or TypeScript, with strong systems-level debugging and profiling skills.

- Deep understanding of distributed systems concepts (caching, queuing, concurrency, resource contention, etc.) and their performance implications.

- Experience designing and implementing load testing, benchmarking, or performance regression frameworks (e.g., Locust, Gatling, k6, custom solutions).

- Familiarity with metrics and tracing systems (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Datadog, etc.) and performance data analysis.

- Experience integrating performance measurement into CI/CD pipelines.

Preferred:

Here are a few qualities we’ve found compatible with our team. If some of this describes you, we’d love to talk.

- You’re curious about how systems behave under real-world load and enjoy building experiments that reveal what’s really happening under the hood.

- You’re an expert in transforming deep technical insights into tools and processes that empower other engineers to build faster, more reliable systems.

title: Data Science Lead
description:
Elliptic is the leader in digital asset decisioning, we have built the most comprehensive platform for efficiently extracting crypto data and intelligence across blockchains with the greatest accuracy.

Our platform’s unrivalled uptime, scalability, depth and breadth of our data and intelligence means exacting organizations choose Elliptic for their compliance, risk management, intelligence operations and blockchain infrastructure needs.

Founded in 2013, Elliptic is headquartered in London with offices in New York, Washington D.C., UAE, Singapore and Tokyo. To learn more, visit www.elliptic.co and follow us on LinkedIn and X .

Do you want to lead a data science team on a problem the industry has not solved yet, while still writing code yourself? Are you excited about building the data foundation for how compliance works when the customer is an autonomous agent rather than a person? Are you looking for a values led company where a small team is trusted with a question that matters commercially in months, not years? 

The impact you will have: 

You will lead data science inside Elliptic's Intelligence team, alongside Intelligence Collection, Research and Investigations, and Professional Services. This is deliberately a player-coach role with a prospect of scaling a team. At first you will lead a small team of data scientists and you are expected to own the team's direction, performance and growth. You will own the evidence for the models your team builds, and you will represent them at Elliptic's model risk governance forum. This is not a compliance tax bolted onto the technical work: it is the reason institutions trust our outputs.

The reason we are hiring a lead as we add more data scientists is that a small team working on an unsolved problem needs someone who intrinsically understands the domain, not a layer of management above it. You will set what this team works on, hire the next people into it, and be the person whose technical judgement the team trusts because you can do the work yourself.

What you will do: 

- Lead and grow the team. Set objectives with your data scientists in the context of company strategy, own their performance and development, and be the manager who has the difficult conversation rather than deferring it.
