title: Forward Deployed Engineer
description:
Mattermost is the leading collaborative workflow platform for defense, intelligence, security, and critical infrastructure. Trusted by the U.S. Department of War and Fortune 500s, our platform runs on-premises and in private clouds, delivering secure messaging, file sharing, workflow automation, audio/screenshare, and project management—all with full data and operational control. Mattermost powers high-stakes workflows across mission planning, real-time, real-world operations, DevSecOps, incident response, and cyber defense—enabling secure collaboration from tactical edge and DDIL environments to enterprise HQ. Teams operate across web, desktop, and mobile, with embedded interoperability for Microsoft Teams, Outlook, and Microsoft 365.

To learn more, visit www.mattermost.com 

About Mattermost Federal 

Mattermost is the leading collaborative workflow platform for defense, intelligence, security, and critical infrastructure. Our platform runs on-premises, in private clouds and in air-gapped networks, and is trusted by defense, government and enterprise customers with strict security and compliance requirements.

About the Role 

We are looking for Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) who want to solve real operational problems alongside mission teams. In this role you will work directly with operators, analysts, and engineers to deploy and build systems that are used every day in mission environments.

This is not a traditional engineering role. You will operate close to the mission, often inside classified environments, working through ambiguity and building solutions that have immediate operational impact.

The problems you will work on here are hard, ambiguous, and consequential.

What You'll Do 

- Work directly with defense and intelligence organizations to understand operational problems

- Deploy and integrate Mattermost in classified and mission-critical environments

- Build plugins, integrations, and automations that enable operational workflows

- Prototype new capabilities quickly and iterate based on operator feedback

- Debug complex systems operating in constrained environments

- Help shape the evolution of the Mattermost platform based on mission needs

You will move between writing code, deploying infrastructure, and working directly with operators, often within the same week. Travel is typically approximately one week per month onsite with customers.

What We're Looking For 

- Strong engineering ability (Go, Python, TypeScript, or similar)

- Comfort working across the full stack from infrastructure to applications

- Ability to solve open-ended technical problems

- Strong communication skills with both engineers and operators

- Willingness to travel approximately one week per month

Nice to Have 

- Experience working with DoD, IC, or national security organizations

- Experience deploying systems in secure or classified environments

- Familiarity with Kubernetes, distributed systems, and APIs

- Experience building integrations or operational tooling

AI-Forward Engineering 

Mattermost Federal is aggressively adopting AI-enabled workflows across mission operations. FDEs will be among the first engineers deploying and operationalizing AI capabilities in secure environments, including:

- AI agents that summarize operational channels and generate SITREPs

- AI-assisted mission timelines and decision logs

- Knowledge retrieval across operational history

- AI tools that help operators understand fast-moving mission data

Why This Role Exists 

The best software is built close to the problem. Forward Deployed Engineers at Mattermost Federal work directly with the people using the systems we build. You will see problems firsthand, build solutions quickly, and deploy them into environments where reliability, security, and speed matter.

Compensation 

Mattermost takes a market-based approach to pay. Actual compensation may vary based on location, skills, experience, qualifications, and market conditions.

Mattermost offers a remote-first work environment with medical, dental, and vision coverage. You’ll also receive unlimited PTO plus company holidays, a work from home stipend, an annual learning and development budget for conferences, certifications, and courses, paid parental leave for all parents, and a 401(k) plan.

Canada Eligibility & Compliance 

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in Canada without current or future sponsorship.

This role may require obtaining and maintaining a government security clearance or equivalent designation (such as Reliability Status or Secret clearance under Canada's Controlled Goods Program), depending on customer engagement. Candidates must meet eligibility requirements to be considered. 

Given Mattermost's work with U.S. defense and government customers, some positions may also require compliance with U.S. export control laws, including EAR and ITAR, which can apply to non-U.S. based employees working on covered technical data. For more information, visit the Bureau of Industry and Security and the Directorate of Defense Trade Controls. 

Mattermost is an EEO Employer, we are a remote-first, open-source company.

We are continually working to expand our hiring in more countries and regions, ensuring compliance with local laws and regulations, which takes time.

Mattermost values your unique perspective—we welcome all applicants. We encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply and are committed to assessing candidates based on their skills and qualifications. We do not tolerate discrimination against staff or applicants based on race, religion, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy status, veteran status, or other personal characteristics.

If you require accommodations during the interview process, please let us know—we’re happy to assist.

title: Internal Audit Senior Specialist
description:
About Nu 

Nu serves more than 143 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page 

Audit Senior Specialist 

About Us 

Nu is one of the largest digital financial platforms in the world, with more than 127 million customers across Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia. Guided by our mission to fight complexity and empower people, we are redefining financial services in Latin America and this is still just the beginning of the purple future we're building.

Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: NU), we combine proprietary technology, data intelligence, and an efficient operating model to deliver financial products that are simple, accessible, and human.

Our impact has been recognized by global rankings such as Time 100 Companies, Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies, and Forbes World’s Best Bank. Visit our institutional page https://international.nubank.com.br/careers/ 

About the role 

You will be the statutory Head of Internal Audit for Nubank's European entity and the primary Internal Audit point of contact for the local regulator. As Nubank builds its regulated European operation, independent assurance is what earns and keeps the trust of the regulator and the governance bodies — you own that from day one.

This is not a role that supervises other people doing the work. It is a full hands-on, build-from-scratch role: for the first 12–18 months you will operate largely on your own, performing and leading the audits yourself, with the support of Nubank's global Internal Audit team and additional resources over time as the function matures. You'll report functionally into Nubank's global Internal Audit leadership, preserving Internal Audit's independence and maintaining direct access to the entity's Audit and Risk Committees.

You will build a modern, data-driven audit function — one that leans on automation, analytics and AI rather than traditional checklist auditing — while partnering with a young, fast-scaling business where governance and controls are still being built. Your goal: stand up and run a credible Internal Audit function that gives the Committees and the local regulator confidence that Nubank is growing in a healthy, sustainable way.

You'll be responsible for 

- Acting as the statutory Head of Internal Audit for the European entity, representing Internal Audit before the local regulator and reporting independently into Nubank's global Internal Audit leadership and the relevant Committees.

- Owning the entity's Internal Audit universe and risk assessment — a dynamic view of key risks across products, digital asset initiatives, financial crime, governance and internal-control frameworks.

- Designing and executing the audit plan, and coordinating closely with Nubank's global Internal Audit function and the hubs in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia.

- Performing and leading end-to-end audits hands-on — not only scoping and coordinating fieldwork, but often running the testing yourself — covering fintech/digital banking products, digital assets and related infrastructure, AML/financial-crime obligations, and governance, risk and control frameworks.

- Coordinating Internal Audit's contribution to supervisory interactions with the local regulator, being comfortable explaining clearly what Internal Audit does before any regulator, and proactively communicating emerging risks.

- Engaging the governance bodies — Audit Committee and Risk Committee — with clear, concise, impact-oriented reporting.

- Building trust-based relationships with local senior management and second-line risk/compliance partners, operating as a trusted challenger and advisor while preserving Internal Audit's independence.

- Promoting the use of technology, data and AI in the audit work — continuous auditing routines, data analytics, AI-assisted testing and documentation — to increase coverage and enable predictive risk monitoring.

- Acting as a culture carrier for Nubank's Internal Audit, keeping the local function fully integrated into the global audit vision and standards.

- Over time, and consistent with business and regulatory needs, designing, building and leading an appropriately resourced Internal Audit function for the entity.

We are looking for a person who has 

Experience and background

- A solid Internal Audit background in financial services (as an internal or external auditor); senior second-line/compliance profiles are welcome when grounded in prior Internal Audit experience.

- Experience with the Swiss or European regulatory framework.

- Meaningful experience in fintech or banking.

- Experience engaging governance bodies, specifically Audit and Risk Committees.

- Proven knowledge of fintech/digital-banking business models, AML/financial-crime controls and investigations, and traditional banking products and infrastructure.

Ways of working and skills

- High ownership and autonomy

- A genuinely hands-on posture

- A builder mindset

- A data-driven approach to audit: experience with data and analytics in audit or risk work; hands-on SQL/Python is a strong plus and a good signal of fit, and a strong appetite to work with data-driven testing is essential.

Cultural openness and humility

- Ability to analyze end-to-end processes and controls across finance, credit, payments, AML, information security, technology and governance, connecting the details to the overall risk profile.

- Excellent written and verbal communication, explaining complex topics clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, including regulators and senior executives.

- Strong stakeholder management — influencing senior leaders, challenging constructively and building trust across the three lines of defense.

- German is required — the local regulator operates in German and there is no intermediary for regulatory interaction, so working proficiency in German is needed. Fluent English is also required.

Nice to have

- Experience with digital assets — crypto and stablecoins. (Digital-assets experience is a plus, not a requirement)

- No specific certification is required (CIA, ACCA, CISA, etc. are welcome but not mandatory).

Location for this opportunity 

- Zug, Switzerland

Our Benefits 

- Chance of earning equity at Nubank

- Health Insurance Allowance for you and your dependents

- Pension Plan

- Accident Insurance

- Daily Sickness Benefits

- Life Insurance & Death Benefits

- NuCare – Employee Assistance Programme, available 24/7 for you and your dependents

- NuLanguage – Language Course Program

- International Travel Insurance for business trips

- Work-from-home Allowance and office equipment for working from home

- Parking space at the Zug office

Work Model for this Role

title: Propellant Quality Control Engineer
description:
We are looking for a Propellant Quality Control Engineer to ensure the quality, consistency, and traceability of the materials and processes used to manufacture our solid propellants. Working closely with the Lead Propellant Manager, laboratory technicians, propulsion engineers, manufacturing, and suppliers, you will define and execute quality-control activities from incoming raw materials through to finished propellant.

This is a hands-on role for someone who combines strong technical judgement with a disciplined approach to measurement, documentation, investigation, and process control. Your work will help ensure that propellant development and production remain safe, repeatable, and aligned with the required performance standards.

About us 

We’re a Germany-based rocketry startup currently in stealth mode, scaling up rapidly to meet the demand for high-performance, reliable, and scalable solid propulsion technologies for space and defense applications.

We are already launching suborbital and ballistic rockets on a regular basis, generating significant revenue and applying our knowledge toward the development of an orbital rocket.

We are working hard to build something truly spectacular.

To thrive here you will need to be comfortable working at pace, with the autonomy to make decisions and execute on them quickly. If you’re excited by hard technical challenges and want a role where you will make a real difference each day to the future of the company, we may be the place for you.

At our company, job titles and career progression are earned, not determined by years of experience alone. They reflect the responsibility you take on and the dedication you bring to each project. If you’re ready to rise to the challenge, we’d love to hear from you.

Key responsibilities 

- Define and perform quality-control checks for raw materials, intermediate products, and finished propellant.

- Develop and maintain inspection plans, test methods, acceptance criteria, sampling requirements, and quality records.

- Review laboratory and production data to identify trends, variation, out-of-specification results, and emerging process issues.

- Lead or support investigations into non-conformances, deviations, material issues, and unexpected test results.

- Maintain clear traceability of materials, batches, samples, equipment, results, and technical decisions.

- Work with the Lead Propellant Manager and manufacturing teams to improve process capability, measurement quality, and production consistency.

What we are looking for 

- Experience in quality control, quality engineering, laboratory testing, or process control within a chemical, aerospace, manufacturing, or other regulated environment.

- A degree in chemical engineering, chemistry, materials science, mechanical engineering, or a related discipline.

- Strong understanding of measurement systems, test methods, sampling, data review, and technical documentation.

- Experience investigating non-conformances, identifying root causes, and implementing corrective actions.

- A methodical and detail-oriented approach to safety, traceability, data integrity, and compliance.

- Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with laboratory, engineering, manufacturing, quality, and supplier teams.

title: Senior Applied AI Engineer, Document Intelligence
description:

About the role

For 40 years Vertican has buildt software that runs law firms. One year ago we created a new modern AI platform for document automation (processing/extraction/redacting) which our customers have been adopting faster than any product we've ever had. Our suite of AI-enabled products save customers thousands of hours each week by processing high volumes of documents with precision and speed.The AI team is growing and we'd like you to join.

We are hiring an engineer to own the document processing pipelines end to end: design, benchmarking, experimenting with new architectures and tools, threshold required for deploying a new pipeline, etc.

We believe it's important to build our own tooling to help us run, improve, and measure our applications. Therefore, the ideal candidate thinks outside the box on how to not just build the product/pipeline, but also the tooling needed around it.

You will be the first dedicated ML hire on the product taking over from the engineering manager who build the current solution and will work directly with the founding engineering team.

This is a senior, hands-on individual-contributor role, but we are small team and you'll be involved in design, planning, roadmapping, and architectural decisions.

What you will do

Design the pipelines. Own the architecture of the extraction-to-posting pipelines: page classification, field extraction, candidate retrieval, claim matching, confidence gating and the hand-off to human review, etc. Decide where rules end and models begin, and what each stage must guarantee to the next, what the separation of concerns are, etc.

We have different pipelines for different document types and expect that at any given point in time we may have new ones emerge and may consolidate others.

Evaluate new systems before we adopt them. Run structured trials of candidate components and recommend what to keep. Examples include probabilistic record linkage (Splink), Azure AI Content Understanding and Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI and Foundry-hosted models, and LLM agents with tools. Similarly, test new models with the existing pipeline as they are relased from the frontier labs.

Build the evaluation process. You'll own the process of evaluating false positives, false negatives, errors of ommission, etc, that we ultimately use to determine if we should upgrade the pipeline. 

Ship and operate. Take components from trial to production in our python workers on the cloud, instrument them, watch cost and quota, and diagnose the cases reviewers send back.

Set direction. Work with leadereship on the planing for accuracy, cost improvement, and overall product improvements.

What we are looking for

Required 

- 6+ years building ML or data-intensive systems, at least 3 of them owning a production pipeline whose output people acted on.

- Solid backend engineering understanding and ideally cloud architecture understanding.

- Ideally hands-on experience with document understanding: OCR or layout models, field extraction from scanned PDFs, or intelligent document processing products.

- Experience with entity resolution or record linkage at scale (Splink, Dedupe, Zingg, or your own blocking-and-scoring system) against databases of hundreds of thousands of rows.

- You have designed an evaluation from scratch: built a labeled ground-truth set, chosen the metrics, and defended a threshold to a non-technical stakeholder.

- Production experience with LLM APIs, including structured output, tool calling and cost or rate-limit management; you can say when an LLM is the wrong tool.

- Strong Python and SQL. Comfortable reading Postgres query plans and writing the raw query when the ORM gets in the way.

- Engineering/Scientist mindset: you are scientific about testing the pipeline and how results are interpeted/presented.

Nice to have 

- Azure AI services (Content Understanding, Document Intelligence, Azure OpenAI, Foundry) or the AWS and GCP equivalents.

- Financial document processing: checks, remittance advices, lockbox files, payment matching, or accounts receivable automation.

- Exposure to collections, legal operations or other regulated workflows handling PII.

- Probabilistic matching theory (Fellegi-Sunter) or active-learning labeling workflows.

- Experience building human-review tooling or feedback loops that feed back into training and evaluation data.

Small team, direct access to large datasets, weekly planning, daily standup, everyone remote in US timezones.

- A small team of tight-knit, like-minded people passionate about high quality software

- Competitive compensation, commensurate with a senior individual-contributor role.

title: Senior Data Scientist, People Analytics & Research

Employee listening and survey analysis are part of the mix, but the heart of the role is rigorous inferential research on observational people data. title: Embedded Controls Software Engineer
description:
At DeWarmte, we develop technology that helps homes move away from gas. Our heat pumps combine hardware, embedded control software, cloud services and data – and the quality of the software connecting those elements directly determines how well our products perform in customers’ homes.

We are looking for an experienced Embedded Controls Software Engineer to develop and evolve the software that operates our heat pumps and, increasingly, a broader range of connected energy devices. As part of our Control & Data team, you will work directly on production software, refine control algorithms, improve product performance and help shape the next generation of our embedded software platform.

This is a hands-on engineering role at the intersection of software, hardware, control engineering and energy systems. You will work on technology that is already operating in customers’ homes while building the technical foundations for future products and use cases.

Your mission

Build reliable, efficient and extensible control software that enables our products to operate intelligently in an increasingly connected and flexible energy system.
You will inherit working software already deployed in the field. Your job is to understand it deeply, maintain and improve it, and progressively evolve its architecture to support new products, control strategies and regulatory requirements.
Together with the Lead Controls & Data Engineer and our Hardware R&D team, you will help build an embedded software platform that can scale with DeWarmte’s ambitions.

What you will do

Maintain and improve our control software

- Work directly in the production code that controls our heat pumps.

- Design, build, test and deploy new control functionality.

- Develop, refine and validate control algorithms to improve product performance, stability, safety, energy efficiency and customer comfort.

- Use operational data and real-world measurements to understand product behaviour and identify opportunities for improvement.

- Diagnose complex behaviour across software, electronics, sensors, hydraulics and the physical installation.

- Improve automated testing, simulation, observability and release practices.

- Help ensure reliable operation of both newly developed products and our existing installed fleet.

Evolve our embedded software platform

- Contribute to the architecture and technical evolution of our on-device software stack.

- Gradually migrate our existing Python-based control software to a compiled systems programming language, with Rust as the preferred direction.

- Improve software maintainability, runtime reliability, resource efficiency and testability while preserving proven control behaviour.

- Develop and extend our over-the-air (OTA) software update mechanisms, enabling reliable and controlled software deployments across our connected device fleet.

- Contribute to the development of our next-generation embedded hardware configuration, working closely with our Hardware R&D colleagues on hardware-software integration and platform design.

- Establish clear interfaces and reusable software components that allow the platform to evolve without unnecessary complexity.

Expand our control capabilities

- Extend our control software to support new devices, product configurations and energy management use cases.

- Develop control strategies that respond to external signals, dynamic energy prices, grid constraints and demand-side flexibility opportunities.

- Translate evolving regulatory requirements and interoperability standards into robust, testable software functionality.

- Develop interfaces that enable our products to interact with external energy management systems, other connected devices and third-party services.

- Help balance energy efficiency, customer comfort, equipment longevity and flexibility in our control strategies.

Work across the product

You will collaborate closely with colleagues in hardware, software, data, product development, assembly, installation and service. You will help resolve immediate customer and operational issues while protecting the long-term quality of our software platform.

You will actively contribute to technical discussions, code reviews, documentation and shared engineering practices, ensuring that our software can be understood, maintained and evolved by the entire team.

What success looks like in your first month

- You develop a solid understanding of our existing heat pump control software, development workflows and embedded environment.

- You become familiar with the physical behaviour of our products and the interfaces between software and hardware.

- You actively contribute to day-to-day software development, debugging and maintenance.

- By the end of your first month, you are able to independently drive the development of new control functionality, with support from the wider team where needed.

In the following months

- You take increasing technical ownership of our on-device control software.

- You independently design, implement, test and deploy improvements to our control algorithms and functionality.

- You contribute to measurable improvements in product reliability, performance and software quality.

- You help define and validate the architecture for migrating our Python-based control software to a compiled language.

- You begin extending and improving our OTA software update mechanisms.

As the role develops

- You drive the progressive migration of our control software towards a modern, robust and maintainable systems programming stack.

- New control functionality can be delivered predictably and safely across our installed fleet.

- You contribute to the design, development and validation of our next-generation embedded hardware and software platform.

- Our control software supports an increasingly diverse range of devices, regulatory requirements, interoperability standards and energy management use cases.

- Critical software components are well documented, thoroughly tested and understood by more than one engineer.

- You become a key technical contributor to the evolution of DeWarmte’s control software platform.

What we are looking for

Essential experiences and skills

- Several years of hands-on software engineering experience, ideally at mid- to senior level, including experience with production systems.

- Practical experience developing, implementing and validating control algorithms for physical products, machines or energy systems.

- Practical experience with HVAC systems, thermal energy systems or controllable energy assets in the context of demand-side flexibility, including an understanding of their physical behaviour and operational constraints.

- Experience developing software in embedded or hardware-connected environments.

- Hands-on experience with a modern systems programming language such as Rust or Go. Extensive experience with C, C++ or comparable low-level languages is also relevant, provided you are willing and able to transition to a modern systems programming stack.

- A good working knowledge of Python and the ability to understand, maintain and evolve an existing Python codebase.

- Strong engineering fundamentals, including version control, automated testing, code reviews and CI/CD workflows.

- The ability to reason across software, hardware and physical-system behaviour and systematically diagnose complex problems.

- Comfort working with modern LLM-based and agentic software development tools and workflows, while maintaining a high standard of engineering quality, code review and verification.

- The ability to take functionality through the complete development lifecycle, from design and implementation to testing, deployment and real-world operation.

Additional valuable experience

- Embedded Linux development, particularly experience with Yocto or Buildroot, custom system images and embedded Linux deployment workflows.

- Direct experience developing control software or control algorithms for heat pumps.

- Experience with OTA software updates, connected-device fleet management and reliable software deployment to remotely operated devices.

- Familiarity with industrial or energy-sector communication protocols, interoperability standards and regulatory requirements.

- Experience with simulation, hardware-in-the-loop testing, control system modelling or optimisation.

- Experience with front-end paradigms and languages, whether web-based or native, preferably using modern JavaScript or TypeScript frameworks.

We do not expect you to bring experience in every one of these areas. We value strong software and control engineering fundamentals, intellectual curiosity and the ability to quickly develop a deep understanding of complex physical products.

How you work

- You take ownership of problems from initial investigation through to implementation, validation and deployment.

- You enjoy working at the intersection of software and the physical world and are interested in understanding why a system behaves the way it does.

- You solve urgent problems without allowing permanent workarounds to become the architecture.

- You balance pragmatic improvements today with the technical investments needed to scale tomorrow.

- You use modern development tools, including AI-assisted and agentic workflows, to work effectively without compromising reliability or your understanding of the software.

- You explain complex technical matters clearly to people with different backgrounds.

- You share knowledge by default and build software that other engineers can intuitively understand, easily test and safely change.

- You are comfortable switching between debugging a specific installation, refining a control algorithm and developing the architecture for our next generation of products.

What you will get

- Direct influence on technology that contributes to the energy transition.

- Ownership of software that sits at the heart of a real physical product.

- The opportunity to work on challenging problems at the intersection of embedded software, control engineering and energy systems.

- The opportunity to shape the transition towards a modern embedded software platform

- A role that starts deeply hands-on and grows into broader technical ownership and architectural responsibility.

- Close collaboration with colleagues across the complete product lifecycle.

What we offer

- A monthly gross salary between €4.500 and €6.000, based on full-time.

- 27 vacation days plus 8% holiday allowance.

- Participation in our SAR (Stock Appreciation Rights) programme.

- Plenty of ownership and responsibility from day one.

- The opportunity to shape products that directly contribute to the energy transition.

- A talented, ambitious, and highly collaborative team.

- A healthy daily lunch at the office.

- Laptop and everything you need to do your best work.

- Regular team events, company drinks, our annual beach day, and winter trip.

- Lots of room to grow, develop yourself, and make a lasting impact.

Interested?

Do you want to build intelligent control software for real physical products and help shape the next generation of connected, energy-efficient heating and energy systems?

We would like to meet you!

Compensation: €4.5K – €6K per month

Le Centre de Génie Industriel (CGI) développe des activités d’enseignement et de recherche autour de la modélisation, du pilotage et de l’amélioration des systèmes industriels et organisationnels, dans des contextes complexes et incertains (industrie du futur, supply chain, résilience, etc.).

Contexte et missions 

Les inégalités territoriales d’accès aux soins constituent un enjeu majeur des politiques publiques de santé en France. Elles sont particulièrement marquées dans les territoires ruraux et isolés, caractérisés par une faible densité de population, des distances importantes aux services de santé et une démographie médicale parfois fragile. Dans ces territoires, l’amélioration de l’accès aux soins ne repose pas uniquement sur l’augmentation du nombre de professionnels de santé, mais également sur leur localisation et leur organisation territoriale.

Dans le cadre du projet de recherche MAillage Territorial pour Améliorer l’Accès aux soins dans les zones Rurales et Isolées (MATAARI), l’objectif est de développer des méthodes d’optimisation permettant de concevoir de nouvelles organisations territoriales de l’offre de soins, en tenant compte des contraintes géographiques, démographiques et médicales.

Les indicateurs actuellement utilisés pour caractériser l’accès aux soins, notamment l’Accessibilité Potentielle Localisée (APL) développée par la DREES [1], permettent de prendre en compte simultanément la demande de soins, l’offre médicale et la distance entre les populations et les professionnels de santé. Aujourd’hui, ces indicateurs sont principalement utilisés à des fins de diagnostic et de caractérisation des territoires. L’enjeu de ce stage sera de les intégrer dans un problème d’optimisation afin de déterminer les conditions nécessaires à l’amélioration de l’accessibilité aux soins.

Le stage constituera ainsi une première étape consacrée à la localisation optimale de professionnels de santé, avant une intégration ultérieure de ce problème dans les modèles de districting développés dans le cadre de MATAARI.

Dans un premier temps, le.la candidat.e développera un modèle de Facility Location Problem (FLP) intégrant notamment l’offre et la demande de soins, les indicateurs d’accessibilité, les spécificités territoriales et sociales, qui pourront être éclairées par les travaux de l’équipe interdisciplinaire en sciences humaines et sociales travaillant également sur le projet. Une attention particulière sera portée à la non-linéarité du problème.

Dans un second temps, le modèle de localisation sera adapté dans une perspective d’intégration au problème de districting territorial développé dans le projet MATAARI. Il s’agira d'identifier comment les décisions de localisation de l’offre médicale peuvent être intégrées aux décisions de découpage du territoire afin de construire un modèle hiérarchisé ou intégré.

L’objectif final est ainsi de disposer d’un modèle de localisation autonome pouvant constituer un module d’optimisation de l’offre de soins, intégrable ultérieurement aux modèles de maillage territorial développés par les autres acteurs du projet.

État de l’art 

Les problèmes de localisation d’infrastructures (Facility Location Problems) constituent une famille classique de problèmes de recherche opérationnelle visant à déterminer l’implantation optimale d’un ensemble d’infrastructures afin de répondre à une demande distribuée spatialement [2], [3]

De nombreuses variantes ont été développées, notamment les problèmes de p-median, set covering, maximal covering location problem et capacitated facility location. Ces modèles ont été largement mobilisés dans le domaine de la santé pour étudier l’implantation d’hôpitaux, de centres de soins ou de professionnels de santé [4], [5]

Dans le contexte médical, les modèles de localisation doivent toutefois intégrer des caractéristiques spécifiques : demande hétérogène, capacité limitée des professionnels, accessibilité spatiale, distances maximales, concurrence entre sites et incertitude sur l’offre médicale. Une réflexion sur la définition et la mesure de l’accessibilité permettra de proposer une modélisation plus fine des interactions entre la localisation de l’offre de soins, les distances et les besoins des populations. Le problème étudié dans le cadre de ce stage se situe ainsi à l’intersection des problèmes de localisation, des problèmes d’accessibilité spatiale et des problèmes d’organisation territoriale des soins.

Une seconde dimension concerne le lien avec les problèmes de districting et de territory design [6], [7].

Alors que ces derniers cherchent principalement à construire des territoires cohérents sous différentes contraintes géographiques et démographiques, le couplage avec un problème de localisation permet d'introduire explicitement la question de l'organisation de l'offre de soins au sein de ces territoires.

Ce couplage constitue une étape importante vers le développement d'un modèle de maillage territorial adapté aux spécificités des zones rurales.

Profil recherché 

Nous cherchons un.e candidat.e en M2 ou dernière année d’école d’ingénieurs, spécialisé.e en Recherche Opérationnelle, Optimisation Combinatoire, Informatique ou domaine connexe.

Compétences attendues : 

- Formalisation de problèmes complexes (PL, PLNE)

- Compétences solides en algorithmique et programmation (de préférence Python)

- Bonnes capacités rédactionnelles en français et en anglais pour la documentation et la communication des résultats

Modalités

Durée : 5-6 mois

Lieu : Albi

We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should know how to put it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in.

Our first product is a full-stack platform for launching and running private investment firms, allowing you to run everything from your phone - think Shopify for VC and PE. We handle all the infrastructure: from legal structuring and investor onboarding to KYC/AML, payments, tax, reporting, and exits.

We're already trusted by over 10,000 angels, VCs, and founders. We administer over $750m in assets, covering investments from pre-seed to series E. This includes household names like ElevenLabs, OpenAI, SpaceX, xAI, Anduril, etc. but also new companies creating everything from synthetic brains to small nuclear reactors.

Why we're hiring 

- We are automating a decades old part of the financial services industry. AI pilled builders like you are the beating heart of this plan, because LLMs & agents allow us to turn this services business entirely into software. 

- This is a product role, and your product is how Odin operates. Think of it as our ghostbuster: every operational problem lands with you, you decide what gets fixed, and you ship most of the fixes yourself rather than writing tickets for someone else.

- We're post-PMF, fast-growing, and rolling out new products (fund admin) & geographies (USA). Customer & deal volume is climbing fast.

- Today we're on track for roughly 700 deals a year, with a team of ~20, and we'll process $500m-$750m of investment in 2026 alone.

- The next goal is 7,000 deals a year and billions in annual investment flows.

- We believe this can be achieved with a team of around 50 people. But it will only be possible if we turn human-driven services workflows into software.

- Odin's operations run on around 50 processes, some code and some people, and plenty still held together by spreadsheets. Your job is to take each one apart, question why it exists, then rebuild it or kill it.

- The simplest way to think about it: the numerator is how many deals we close, the denominator is what each deal costs us to run. You'll focus on the denominator, and the right person won't be able to stop themselves thinking about the numerator too.

- We expect the right hire to be spending more time in Claude Code than in Excel, email or anything else.

What you'll own 

- Triage: Every operational problem comes to you before it reaches product and engineering. For each one you decide: scope it so precisely that engineering knows exactly what to build, or build it yourself.

- Cost per deal: There will be big early wins where a whole process can be ripped out and replaced. After that, doubling ops efficiency comes from 150 small changes, and you'll be the one making them.

- Automation: You'll sit with the deal operations team, learn each workflow end to end, then build what replaces it. Most of what you ship you'll build without engineering. What does go to them arrives simple, scoped and usually with a working prototype attached.

- Deleting things and saying no: You decide what belongs in our processes and what doesn't. If a request from sales doesn't scale and isn't highly profitable we don't do it. If a way of working exists for no good reason, you kill it.

- The ops team: You'll lead the core deal operations team, deciding where their time goes while you rebuild the work around them.

What we're looking for 

- You build, not buy: Clear evidence, at work or in your own time, that you've built real solutions with AI with no budget and no engineers. Buying a tool or setting up workflows in Sheets doesn't count. We want to see what you've shipped in Claude Code or similar.

- Founder or product DNA: You've founded something, been early on a founding team, or worked as a product manager. That usually means four or more years of experience and a track record of finishing what you start.

- Systems thinker: You look at any process the way a good product manager looks at a product: What's the job? Why are we doing this at all? What's the smallest, simplest system that achieves the goal? You think about the whole business, not just your corner of it.
A lot of what happens in fund admin is inherited convention, an industry "given", or a constraint of some third party. You should find it physically difficult to accept any of that.

- In the details and extremely on top of things: You understand every single aspect of our systems end to end. You close loops, you chase, you push hard to get things done.

- Numerate: Comfortable with financial mechanics, strong mental arithmetic. You'll be automating a lot of numerical work - carry, allocations, fee calculations, distributions, and the edge cases that make all of them interesting.

- Big plus: regulated financial services background: Fund administration, custody, payments, brokerage, audit, tax or another back office function. Useful, but not required. We care much more about the traits you have and the things you can build than specific skills or experience on your CV.

How we work 

There are five things we care about deeply:

- Reason from the ground up 
Seek to understand what is true by always asking why. Do not trust convention or experts.

- Speed begets speed 
We work fast. Speed compounds, it's the best form of defensibility, and it's energising to be around. If you work slowly, or tolerate slow work around you, you do not belong at Odin.

- Take ownership 
Do not wait for permission to do things. Find the answer, force the thing into existence and hold others to an extremely high standard - the same standard you hold yourself to.

- Brutal honesty 
If work doesn't meet the bar, people need to hear it, and the right people want to.

- Truly excellent customer service 
Be a stickler for detail in every single interaction a customer has with us, and always strive to make this experience better, smoother, faster.

This role is probably not for you if 

- You'd rather write specs and hand tickets to engineers than build the thing yourself;

- You prefer close management of your responsibilities;

- You are risk-averse;

- You want a 9-5;

- You take yourself too seriously;

- You care about working for a company that's raised lots of money rather than one that's extremely capital efficient and focused on building a profitable giant that has a positive economic impact

Salary 

£90k - £120k base, plus a meaningful equity grant. We're flexible on the mix of cash and equity.

Hiring process 

Three stages, usually inside two weeks, with detailed feedback within 24 hours of each one. A call with our Head of People, an in-person session with the founders where you solve a real Odin problem end to end with AI, then a final with the founders. The last two can run on the same day.

Location & ways of working 

We're a London-based team. This role works closely with the founders, product and the wider ops team, and the speed we run at makes that much easier in-person. At least three days a week in the office.

Benefits 

- Health: Private health insurance (Vitality), paid sick leave including support for pregnancy loss and fertility treatments, and access to Spill for mental health support

- Wellness: £1,000 annual budget for health, therapy or fitness

- Parental Leave: Enhanced maternity, adoption, paternity and partner leave

- Pension: 4% employer contribution with salary sacrifice options

- Time Off: 25 days annual leave, 2 wellness days and flexible bank holidays (33 days total)

- Work From Anywhere: Up to 6 weeks per year working from anywhere globally

- Birthday Leave: An additional day of leave

Ready to apply? 

If you're interested in joining our team at Odin, apply here 

When you apply, send us a link to something (or things) you've built with AI. Applicants who do not share anything will not be accepted. 

Compensation: £90K – £120K • Offers Equity

Why we’re hiring 

- We're post-PMF and revenue generating, launching in the US ahead of a Series A. Early enough that you'll shape how engineering works here, late enough that you're not gambling on whether the product works.

- You'll own significant parts of the product and ship the things customers feel most. It's a regulated platform moving money across multiple jurisdictions, so the work has to be right and it still has to be fast.

You think the impact of AI on engineering is overstated. You'd rather be handed a fully specified ticket than question the brief. Or the learning curve across finance, compliance and multiple jurisdictions sounds like a chore rather than the interesting part.

The people who do well here find that last bit genuinely interesting. Understanding how capital actually moves, and what the rules allow in each jurisdiction, is most of what makes this product hard to build and hard to copy.

title: ChatGPT Performance Engineer
description:
About the Team 

We bring OpenAI's technology to the world through products like ChatGPT and the OpenAI API.

We seek to learn from deployment and distribute the benefits of AI, while ensuring that this powerful tool is used responsibly and safely. Safety is more important to us than unfettered growth.

About the Role 

OpenAI is looking for an experienced Performance Engineer to help us scale the performance, reliability, and efficiency of our systems. In this role, you'll apply deep technical expertise to optimize infrastructure and application-level performance across mission-critical products like ChatGPT and our developer API. You’ll work cross-functionally with teams building core services, training models, and developing real-time user experiences to push our latency, throughput, and cost-efficiency to the next level.

We are looking for engineers who thrive in ambiguous environments, value deep systems understanding, and are motivated by delivering measurable impact. This is a highly technical, individual contributor role focused on root-cause analysis, profiling, instrumentation, and architecture-level performance improvements across our stack.

In this role, you will: 

- 
Analyze and optimize performance across application, middleware, runtime, and infrastructure layers—networking, storage, Python runtime, GPU utilization, and beyond.

- 
Develop tooling and metrics that provide deep observability into system performance.

- 
Collaborate closely with infra, platform, training, and product teams to identify key performance goals and drive systemic improvements.

- 
Influence architecture and design decisions to prioritize latency, throughput, and efficiency at scale.

- 
Lead investigations into high-impact performance regressions or scalability issues in production.

- 
Drive performance testing strategies and help define SLAs/SLOs around latency and throughput for critical systems.

You might thrive in this role if you: 

- 
Have 7+ years of experience in software engineering with a strong track record in performance or reliability of high-scale distributed systems.

- 
Are deeply comfortable with performance profiling tools and tracing systems.

- 
Have experience optimizing performance across one or more layers of the stack (e.g., database, networking, storage, application runtime, GC tuning, Python/Golang internals, GPU utilization).

- 
Have a strong understanding of OS internals, scheduling, memory management, and IO patterns.

- 
Have contributed to observability, benchmarking, or performance-focused infrastructure at scale.

- 
Have demonstrated success navigating ambiguity and aligning stakeholders around performance goals.

- 
Value simplicity, rigor, and collaboration when solving complex systems problems.

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. title: Senior Data Scientist (R14369)
description:
Headquarters: Remote - India

Who We Are 

Oportun (Nasdaq: OPRT) is a mission-driven financial services company that puts its members' financial goals within reach. With intelligent borrowing, savings, and budgeting capabilities, Oportun empowers members with the confidence to build a better financial future. Since inception, Oportun has provided more than $22.7 billion in responsible and affordable credit, saved its members more than $2.5 billion in interest and fees, and helped its members set aside an average of more than $1,800 annually. 

Location Note 

We’re excited to consider talent currently based in India, as well as candidates who are open to relocating to India for this opportunity. Please note that, as this is a "Remote–India" position, the role must be performed from within India. 

The Opportunity 

We're looking for a Senior Data Scientist to support our Marketing Data Science team and accelerate new member growth through predictive modeling and advanced analytics. You'll build prospect targeting and conversion prediction models that help Oportun identify promising prospective members, improve acquisition conversion rates, and reduce customer acquisition cost (CAC). You'll own models end to end—from feature development and validation through production deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement—in partnership with Marketing, Growth, Product, and Engineering. 

What You'll Do 

Your day-to-day 

- You'll develop and deploy machine learning models for prospect targeting and conversion prediction to increase new member acquisition. 

- You'll analyze internal prospect and application funnel data, marketing campaign and engagement data, third-party consumer and alternative data, and credit bureau data to build predictive features and identify growth opportunities. 

- You'll apply statistical and machine learning methods, including logistic regression, gradient boosting, and related techniques, to improve targeting accuracy and conversion rates. 

- You'll own reusable pipelines for data preparation, feature engineering, training, scoring, deployment, and ongoing model monitoring. 

- You'll partner with Marketing, Growth, Product, and Engineering to translate model outputs into actionable acquisition strategies and reliable production workflows. 

- You'll measure model effectiveness and business impact through new member acquisition, targeting accuracy, conversion rates, customer acquisition cost, and production reliability. 

Who You Are 

The right fit looks like this 

- You're a curious, rigorous data scientist who turns complex data into reliable models and practical business decisions. 

- You enjoy ambiguous growth problems, take ownership of outcomes, and balance predictive performance with measurable acquisition impact. 

- You're comfortable navigating complexity and don't wait for perfect information to move forward. 

- You communicate clearly, give direct feedback, and expect the same in return. 

What You Bring 

Skills & experience 

Required 

- 4+ years of experience in data science, machine learning, predictive modeling, or a related field. 

- Strong Python and SQL skills and hands-on experience working with large, complex datasets. 

- Experience applying statistical modeling and machine learning techniques, such as logistic regression and gradient boosting, to business problems. 

- Experience developing, validating, deploying, and monitoring production machine learning models. 

- Experience building reusable data preparation, feature engineering, and model scoring pipelines. 

- Ability to assess model performance, data quality, and business outcomes and communicate clear recommendations. 

- Strong cross-functional collaboration, stakeholder management, and project ownership skills. 

Nice to Have 

- Experience in marketing analytics, customer acquisition, prospect targeting, or conversion propensity modeling. 

- Experience with internal prospect and application funnel data, marketing engagement data, third-party consumer or alternative data, or credit bureau data. 

- Experience with AWS, SageMaker, EMR, Spark SQL, Hive, or similar cloud and large-scale data technologies. 

- Experience in consumer lending, fintech, credit risk, or fraud risk. 

- Advanced degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, Engineering, or a related quantitative discipline. 

- Experience using AI-assisted tools to improve modeling, coding, documentation, or research workflows. 

Our AI Mindset 

We build with AI. We lead with judgment. 

AI isn't a feature here. It's how we work. 

We're excited about what AI makes possible, and we're looking for people who share that curiosity. You don't need to be an expert. You need to be open to experimenting , willing to learn, and able to apply new tools in ways that actually move the needle. 

In this role, you'll be encouraged to explore AI tools, find practical use cases for your function, and bring ideas for working smarter. We believe the best outcomes come when human judgment and AI capability work together. 

Why Oportun 

What's in it for you 

Oportun offers a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to support your physical, financial, and professional well-being. Benefits vary by country of employment. 

Some of the benefits available to eligible employees include: 

India Benefits: 

Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance. 

Provident Fund; Life & Accident Insurance. 

Internet, Fuel, Meal & Telephone Allowances. 

Eligibility and plan details vary by location and employment status. To learn more about Oportun and our benefits, visit oportun.com/careers #LI-REMOTE #LI-SS1 

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and consider all qualified applicants for employment opportunities without regard to race, age, color, religion, gender, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status or any other category protected by the laws or regulations in the locations where we operate. 

California applicants can find a copy of Oportun's CCPA Notice here: https://oportun.com/privacy/california-privacy-notice/ . 

We will never request personal identifiable information (bank, credit card, etc.) before you are hired. We do not charge you for pre-employment fees such as background checks, training, or equipment. If you think you have been a victim of fraud by someone posing as us, please report your experience to the FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3).

RoboService GmbH works at the frontier of robotics. We bring humanoid robots from the lab to manufacturing and logistics companies, where they work real shifts. We program robotics applications and build a platform that enables companies to teach robots new tasks on their own.

What we offer

Als QA Engineer werk je niet aan het eind van de keten, maar middenin onze ontwikkelteams. Je denkt mee vóórdat er code geschreven wordt, test slim waar het telt en bent de brug tussen development, product en de rest van het bedrijf als het om kwaliteit gaat. Je valt onder de Teamlead Frontend en werkt dagelijks samen met de frontend-, mobile- en backendteams.

- Meedenken vanaf het begin. Je schuift aan bij refinements en helpt teams de risico's en impact van een feature te zien voordat ze gaan bouwen; 

- De juiste testaanpak kiezen. Samen met het team bepaal je per feature wat je automatisch test, wat je handmatig test en waarom;

- Adviseren over releases. Je brengt risico's in kaart en geeft een duidelijk advies over de kwaliteit van een release. 

- Inzicht geven. Je verzamelt testdata en laat zien hoe het met de kwaliteit van onze software gaat. 

- Balans bewaken. Je helpt teams de afweging te maken tussen bugs oplossen en nieuwe features bouwen. 

Wat breng je mee 

- Een hbo-werk- en denkniveau, bij voorkeur in informatica, software engineering of iets vergelijkbaars. 

- Minimaal 2 jaar werkervaring, waarvan minimaal 1 jaar als QA Engineer, Software Tester of Test Automation Engineer. 

- Ervaring met het opzetten en uitvoeren van een testaanpak en testplannen. 

- Ervaring met testautomatisering en testframeworks. 

- Je werkt vlot met AI-tools en zet ze gericht in: om sneller en beter te testen en om geautomatiseerde tests op te zetten. 

- Ervaring met werken in een Agile/Scrum-team en met een bugtrackingsysteem, bij voorkeur Jira. 

- Je werkt zelfstandig, durft knopen door te hakken in je eigen werk en geeft gevraagd en ongevraagd advies. 

- Je bent kritisch en analytisch, neemt zelf initiatief en kunt goed schakelen met developers, product en business. 

Pluspunten 

- Je hebt kennis van TypeScript/JavaScript en kunt zelf goed uit de voeten met code. 

- Je kijkt verder dan "werkt het?": ook naar toegankelijkheid, snelheid, veiligheid en meertaligheid. 

- Je hebt ervaring met tests die automatisch meedraaien bij elke codewijziging, en weet hoe je onbetrouwbare tests aanpakt. 

- Je deelt graag kennis en helpt collega's beter te testen. 

- Je hebt ervaring met het testen van mobiele apps.

We zoeken iemand die kwaliteit ziet als iets van het hele team. Je perfectioneert niet alleen je eigen testwerk, maar vraagt je af wat er structureel moet veranderen zodat het hele team beter test. Onze eigen waarden zijn daarbij leidend: Own it , Say it , Make it .

title: Ops Strategy Manager - DE
description:
The company 

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team 

Germany is one of iwoca's core markets, with its own Operations teams across Customer Success, Credit Analysis and Collections. The DE Operations Strategy team is the thought partner to those teams. We exist to understand Operations performance, find where Ops adds the most commercial value, and make the changes that get us there. We're a small team with a startup mindset: we challenge assumptions, prototype quickly, pilot in a lean way, and scale what works.

The role 

As an Operations Strategy Manager, you'll own some of the most important projects in our German Operations, from defining the problem through to rollout, across the whole customer journey from application to recovery. Projects could include:

- Better underwriting. Redesigning how our Credit Analysts work alongside our credit models, so that their judgement systematically improves model decisions rather than working around them.

- AI and automation in Operations. Using AI to give our teams richer customer context and remove low-value work – for example, cutting the time Account Managers spend preparing for calls, or drafting the first version of routine customer communications.

- Smarter task distribution. Rethinking how work is prioritised and split between people and automated processes – from when an Account Manager should call a customer to which customers need a personal conversation at all – so that our teams' time goes where human judgement adds the most value.

- Stronger recoveries. Using our growing book of defaulted loans to work out which contact strategies, payment arrangements and recovery routes lead to the best outcomes – for iwoca and for the customer.

Whatever the project, you'll ground decisions in evidence: designing and running split tests, doing your own analysis, and working with our Data Scientists to get even more out of our data. You'll work with Operations, Product and Engineering to put changes live, share recommendations directly with Operations leadership and the German management team, and be part of iwoca's wider community of Analysts and Data Scientists.

The requirements 

Essential:

- Strategy experience. You've worked in a top-tier strategy consultancy or in a strategic role at a tech or finance company.

- Analytical foundations. You have a strong analytical background, through academic qualifications (such as a STEM degree) and professional experience.

- First-principles thinking. You break complex problems into their core parts, challenge assumptions, and recommend well-reasoned, innovative solutions.

- Execution. You've taken recommendations from concept to execution, with hands-on experience implementing product or process improvements.

- Communication. You distil complex information into clear, engaging messages for a range of stakeholders – from Data Scientists and Operations Managers to C-level.

- AI leverage. You use modern tools, including AI, to improve the quality, speed and rigour of your work, while staying responsible for accuracy and outcomes.

Bonus:

description:

Wir sind EXP Software GmbH: Wir sind ein Team aus rund 25 Softwareentwickler*innen mit Herz, Humor und Leidenschaft für Technologie. Wir bauen explore, eine Agentic-Twin-Plattform, die Unternehmen dabei hilft, komplexe Prozesse durch autonome KI-Agenten abzubilden und zu automatisieren.

title: Software Engineer III | Framework
description:
At ExtraHop , we’re on a mission to protect and empower the connected enterprise. We reveal what is happening in the very infrastructure that sustains businesses, lives, and communities, and ensure the integrity of networks, data, systems, and processes. Organizations rely on ExtraHop to provide visibility into the cyber threats, vulnerabilities, and network performance issues that evade their existing security and IT tools. With this insight, organizations can investigate smarter, stop threats faster, and keep operations running.

Our mission is fueled by a profound social and moral responsibility to be the best at what we do, ensuring a secure world where everyone can thrive. If this sounds like a place you’d like to spend the next chapter of your career, we’d love to hear from you. 

Position Summary 

As a Software Engineer III, you will drive key architectural and technical decisions, lead the design and execution of complex engineering initiatives, and elevate technical standards across the Framework team. You’ll partner closely with principal engineers, product leaders, and cross-functional stakeholders to deliver resilient, scalable, and secure systems that power core ExtraHop products. This role is designed for an experienced engineer who combines deep technical expertise with strong ownership and is motivated to grow their impact through excellent engineering and active collaboration.

Our team builds high-performance network detection and monitoring systems that operate at scale across increasingly complex protocols and data volumes.Our services and features are written primarily in C and C++ with a focus on security, scalability, stability, and reliability. Our team is focussed on enhancing, maintaining and optimizing core components of the system and functional areas related to protocol parsing, metrics publishing, continuous packet capture and Time Series DB. 

This role focuses on designing and optimizing these core systems with an emphasis on performance, reliability and deep protocol awareness. You will work on next generation initiatives including scaling and performance improvement efforts, evolution of our data storage architecture (custom to open-source based) and early steps towards a cloud enabled model. 

Key Responsibilities 

- Design, develop, and maintain high-performance services for ExtraHop's core Framework systems, taking ownership of moderately complex to complex features with limited guidance.

- Work across networking layers to implement and enhance protocol support

- Participate actively in technical design discussions, contribute to architecture decisions within your team, and author clear technical documentation for your work.

- Engage fully in agile development processes, including sprint planning, code reviews, and retrospectives; hold a high bar for code quality and test coverage.

- Collaborate with Product and cross-functional engineering partners such as platform , infrastructure and cloud teams to to define technical roadmaps, break down ambiguous problems, and balance technical debt with delivery.

- Investigate, diagnose, and resolve production and performance issues independently; conduct root-cause analysis and implement preventive measures.

- Contribute to platform modernization efforts and help evaluate and adopt new technologies or frameworks in partnership with senior and principal engineers.

- Participate in on-call rotations and improve system observability, reliability and operational readiness. 

Required Qualifications 

- Bachelor’s degree in STEM field, Computer Science, Engineering, or related degree requiring systematic/analytical thinking

- 4+ years of professional software engineering experience designing, building, and operating production systems at scale

- Strong expertise in C and C++ 

- Experience developing on Linux Systems (multi threading, memory management, IPC etc)

- Proven ability to build and maintain performance critical systems. 

- Proven ability to debug complex issues (eg. using gdb, coredumps, performance tools)

- Strong understanding of networking fundamentals 

- Strong command of data structures, algorithms, and software design principles, with the ability to decompose complex problems into clear, actionable engineering tasks.

- Self-starter who can operate independently, manage competing priorities, and drive work to completion with minimal oversight.

- Excellent collaborator and communicator with a growth mindset and customer-first orientation.

Nice-to-Have Qualifications 

- Experience with network protocols (eg. HTTP, SMB, Kerberos, TLS, Microsoft protocols or similar)

- Exposure to cloud platforms (AWS preferred) or distributed systems

- Experience with observability, on-call practices and production systems

- Scripting experience (Python or similar)

Compensation & Benefits: The salary range for this role is $150,000 – $163,000 per year, plus eligibility for an annual performance-based discretionary bonus and stock option grants. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision coverage (effective day 1), a 401(k) with employer match, flexible PTO, parental leave, and more. 

ABOUT EXTRAHOP 

ExtraHop is reinventing Network Detection and Response (NDR) to offer enterprises unparalleled visibility, context, and control against emerging threats. The platform integrates NDR with Network Performance Management (NPM), Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), and forensics, providing a single, comprehensive solution. By decrypting and analyzing complete packet-level data at wire speed and leveraging cloud-scale machine learning, ExtraHop empowers Security Operations Centers (SOCs) to detect, investigate, and remediate modern cyber risks in real time across their entire hybrid infrastructure, including data center, cloud, and SASE environments.

This comprehensive approach and market innovation have earned ExtraHop unique recognition as the only NDR vendor acknowledged as a leader by all major analyst firms, including the 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant for Network Detection and Response™, the 2025 Forrester® Wave for Network Analysis and Visibility, the 2024 IDC® Marketscape for NDR, and the 2025 Gigamon® Radar Report for Network Detection and Response. Since 2007, ExtraHop has consistently helped organizations worldwide extract in-depth network telemetry and contextual insights, affirming its commitment to protecting and empowering the connected enterprise.

OUR VALUES 

Our culture is rooted in our five Values . These set the expectations for how we work individually and collectively as a team. 

Lead with Purpose: We are driven to deliver results that create a positive impact for our customers, partners, and colleagues.

Act with Integrity: We operate with transparency, authenticity, and always in the best interest of the company. 

Find a Way: We are resourceful, tackle hard problems with a sense of urgency and ownership, and do what it takes to get the job done.

Innovate: We listen to customers, partners, and the market, and respectfully push boundaries and challenge the status quo.

Share Success: We run together, we win together. We value diverse perspectives, hold space for all voices, and achieve the best results as a team. 

BENEFITS 

Employees' wellbeing is top of mind for the ExtraHop team. Employees and their families will have the option to participate in the following benefits:

- Health, Dental, and Vision Benefits

- Flexible PTO, Sick Time Prorated Based on Date of Hire, and All Federal Holidays (US Only) + 3 Days of Paid Volunteer Time

- Non-Commissioned Positions may be eligible to participate in the Annual Discretionary Bonus Plan

- FSA and Dependent Care Accounts + EAP, where applicable

- Educational Reimbursement

- 401k with Employer Match or Pension where applicable

- Pet Insurance (US Only)

- Parental Leave (US Only)

- Hybrid and Remote Work Model

Our people are our most important competitive advantage, leading the charge against cyber criminals. Join the fight today! 

To learn more, visit our website or follow us on LinkedIn .

description:
Bloomreach is building the world’s premier agentic platform for personalization .We’re revolutionizing how businesses connect with their customers, building and deploying AI agents to personalize the entire customer journey.

- We're taking autonomous search mainstream, making product discovery more intuitive and conversational for customers, and more profitable for businesses.

We power personalization for more than 1,400 global brands, including American Eagle, Sonepar, and Pandora.

Become a Senior Data Engineer for Bloomreach! 

Join our newly formed Datacraft team — the team building the next-generation data platform that powers internal Databricks, the Loomi Marketing Agent with Data Insights capability for Bloomreach Marketing platform. Your engineering work will directly impact how hundreds of enterprise customers access, understand, and activate their Bloomreach data internally and with data share in Databricks and BigQuery.

The base salary range for this position at the P3 / Senior Software Engineer level is CZK 1 300 000 - CZK 1 600 000. The pay range actually offered will take into account a variety of potential factors considered in compensation, including but not limited to skills, qualifications, geographic location, accomplishments, experience, credentials, internal equity and business needs, and may vary from the range listed above. Working in one of our Central European offices (Bratislava, Brno or Prague) or from home on a full-time basis, you'll become a core part of the Engineering team.

What challenge awaits you? 

You will join the Datacraft team as one of its founding engineers. Datacraft is a new team in the Engagement pillar, established to tackle three interconnected domains:

- Data Warehouses (~60% of team domain) — making Bloomreach data first-class in customer Databricks. The strategic goal for 27 is to use Databricks to exponentially accelerate data adoption — both for customers who want their data outside Bloomreach and for Bloomreach itself to build analytics faster.

- Dashboards & Analytics Stack (~20%) — moving Marketing reporting and dashboarding from the proprietary stack onto Databrick.

Datacraft is an AI-first team. We believe code is a commodity and expect every engineer to fluently use coding agents (e.g., Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, Gemini CLI) as a core part of their daily workflow. The ability to leverage AI tooling to accelerate development, prototyping, and problem-solving is not optional — it's foundational. We rely heavily on knowledge graphs and spec driven development. 

As a P3 (Senior) engineer at Bloomreach you are an independent professional — expert in at least one component, able to decompose objectives into tasks, and lead small projects end-to-end with minimal day-to-day guidance.

Your job will be to: 

- a. Build the Databricks data platform — Design data pipelines (Kafka → Flink -> GCS Iceberg → Databricks) following medallion architecture using Databricks notebooks and Spark Declarative Pipeline. Own data models and ETL mutations for ID resolution and consent semantics. Maintain orchestration (Airflow / Cloud Composer) and monitoring.

- b. Co-build dashboards & analytics stack — Design canonical metrics and models on Databricks, support semantic layers and BI tools (Cube, Looker Studio), ensure tight Marketing Agent (Insights skill) integration.

Our tech stack 

Python, Go, Kafka, Databricks, Airflow, Flink (Java), GCP, Mongo, Redis, Airflow, DataProc, Spark, Apache Flink, Databricks, Kubernetes, Terraform, Grafana, Prometheus, PagerDuty, Sentry, OpenTelemetry, GitLab CI/CD, Claude Code

Your success story 

30 Days: Understand the Datacraft domain, complete onboarding, set up your dev environment, and get oriented on Databricks architecture and Marketing Agent.

90 Days: Ship your first pipeline, data model, or orchestration improvement to production. Join architecture discussions and the on-call rotation.

180 Days: Own a component end-to-end. Make informed trade-off decisions independently. Contribute to measurable team goals.

You have the following experience and qualities: 

Professional experience 

- Solid data engineering background with strong SQL and data modeling skills (star/snowflake schemas, slowly changing dimensions, partitioning/clustering, etc.).

- Hands-on experience building production-grade data pipelines on Databricks and GCP , ideally involving Flink, Iceberg , Spark on DataProc .

- Experience with orchestration and workflow tools — specifically Airflow / Cloud Composer — and comfort working with DAG-based systems for scheduled and event-driven jobs.

- Familiarity with open table formats (Iceberg preferred, Delta Lake / Hudi acceptable) and how they interact with query engines and DWH platforms.

- Strong programming skills in Python (preferred); Scala/Java/Go also relevant.

- Good understanding of data quality, lineage, and observability (monitoring SLAs/SLOs, detecting missing/late loads, backfilling strategies).

- Ability to work across product and engineering teams, turning fuzzy problem statements into incremental, shippable slices.

Strongly preferred 

- Background in marketing analytics, CDPs, or BI/semantic layers (Looker, dbt, Cube).

- Experience with Snowflake or Databricks or BigQuery .

- Experience with spec driven development, knowledge graphs, agentic harnesses or AI-powered analytics 

Personal qualities 

Ownership & accountability · Sharp and Product thinking · Clear communication · Bias for reliability · Continuous improvement mindset · Comfortable remote-first in Central Europe.
